column2: The liquid in young pitchers that haven't opened is clear, so you can drink it when thirsty in the forest. They say monkeys drink it too.

column1: 보르네오 사람들은 이 항아리에 찹쌀을 채워 쪄 먹습니다. 잎 향이 배어 그릇째 먹는 밥이 됩니다.
column2: The people of Borneo fill these pitchers with sticky rice and steam them. The fragrance of the leaf soaks in — rice you eat bowl and all.

column1: 보르네오 사람들은 이 항아리에 찹쌀을 채워 쪄 먹어요. 잎 향이 배어 그릇째 먹는 밥이 돼요.
column2: The people of Borneo fill these pitchers with sticky rice and steam them. The fragrance of the leaf soaks in — rice you eat bowl and all.

column1: 줄기의 흰 가루가 햇볕을 되쏘아 몸이 타지 않게 하고, 다육 잎에 물을 담아 몇 달 가뭄을 견딥니다.
column2: The white powder on its trunk reflects the sun so it doesn't burn, and its fleshy leaves hold water to survive months of drought.

column2: The white powder on its trunk reflects the sun so it doesn't burn, and its fleshy leaves hold water to survive months of drought.

column1: 산 사람들은 이 나무의 속 빈 가지를 깎아 화살통을 만듭니다. 퀴버라는 이름이 거기서 왔습니다.
column2: The mountain people carve its hollow branches into arrow quivers. That's where the name "quiver tree" comes from.

column2: The mountain people carve its hollow branches into arrow quivers. That's where the name "quiver tree" comes from.

column2: A tree with branches spread like a star stands alone on a barren rocky hill. Paint it against the sun when the yellow flowers bloom and the star seems to burn.

column2: A tree with branches spread like a star stands alone on a barren rocky hill. Paint it against the sun when the yellow flowers bloom and the star seems to burn.

column1: 나무가 이렇게 서 있는 곳은 땅이 몹시 메마른 곳이니, 물통을 넉넉히 채운 뒤에 이 언덕을 넘어야 합니다.
column2: Where these trees grow, the land is bone-dry, so fill the water casks well before crossing this hill.

column2: They say he was the son King Minos's queen bore to a white bull that rose from the sea. Every nine years Athens sent seven pairs of youths to the labyrinth as its food.

column2: They say Theseus brought down the bull-headed one bare-handed, or with a short sword. Against something that charges with horns, don't meet it head-on — step aside and strike.

column2: The palace walls still show youths grabbing an angry bull's horns and somersaulting over its back. To the people of this island, the bull was both god and terror.

column2: They say a troll turns to stone the moment sunlight touches it. The big man-shaped boulders on the mountainside are said to be trolls who stayed out too late and saw the sun.

column2: Trolls hate church bells and leave valleys where bells ring. The villagers hang iron and crosses at their doors.

column2: The Norwegians say trolls are strong but dim, so keep one busy with riddles and wordplay until morning and you win.

column2: On a windless day, a long V-shaped wake splits the water across the middle of the loch. It's no boat's wake.

column2: The water is dark red with peat, so you can't see a foot below the surface. If a long-necked beast lives in water like this, it must be thanks to the runs of salmon.

column2: Strings are stretched along a bamboo tube and plucked with the fingertips for a clear sound. Every evening young men and women sit facing each other and trade love songs to it.

column2: Bamboo straws are stuck in a jar of rice wine, and everyone takes turns sucking from them. They say they're hurt if a guest refuses the straw.

column1: 바깥의 무서운 소문과 달리 이들은 손님을 정중히 맞습니다. 다만 마을의 관습법인 「아닷」을 어기면 엄하게 다스리니 먼저 어른에게 묻는 것이 좋겠습니다.
column2: Despite the frightening rumors outside, they welcome guests courteously. But they deal harshly with anyone who breaks "adat," the village's customary law, so it's best to ask the elders first.

column1: 바깥의 무서운 소문과 달리 이들은 손님을 정중히 맞아요. 다만 마을의 관습법인 「아닷」을 어기면 엄하게 다스리니 먼저 어른에게 묻는 것이 좋겠어요.
column2: Despite the frightening rumors outside, they welcome guests courteously. But they deal harshly with anyone who breaks "adat," the village's customary law, so it's best to ask the elders first.

column1: 호수 잉어를 안달리만 열매와 고추, 강황으로 조려 혀가 얼얼합니다. 이 열매는 산초처럼 혀끝이 저리게 합니다.
column2: Lake carp braised with andaliman berries, chili and turmeric leaves your tongue tingling. The berry numbs the tip of the tongue like Sichuan pepper.

column1: 호수 잉어를 안달리만 열매와 고추, 강황으로 조려 혀가 얼얼해요. 이 열매는 산초처럼 혀끝이 저리게 해요.
column2: Lake carp braised with andaliman berries, chili and turmeric leaves your tongue tingling. The berry numbs the tip of the tongue like Sichuan pepper.

column1: 집 지붕이 배 모양으로 양 끝이 치솟았고, 박공에는 물소 머리와 붉고 검은 덩굴 무늬를 새겼습니다. 못 하나 쓰지 않고 지었습니다.
column2: The roofs of the houses are boat-shaped, both ends soaring, and the gables are carved with buffalo heads and red-and-black vine patterns. Built without a single nail.

column1: 집 지붕이 배 모양으로 양 끝이 치솟았고, 박공에는 물소 머리와 붉고 검은 덩굴 무늬를 새겼어요. 못 하나 쓰지 않고 지었어요.
column2: The roofs of the houses are boat-shaped, both ends soaring, and the gables are carved with buffalo heads and red-and-black vine patterns. Built without a single nail.

column1: 숲 사람은 팔이 다리보다 훨씬 길어 땅을 걷기보다 나무 사이를 흔들며 건너갑니다. 밤마다 나뭇가지를 꺾어 새 잠자리를 엮습니다.
column2: The forest man's arms are far longer than his legs, so he swings between trees rather than walking on the ground. Every night he breaks branches and weaves a new bed.

column1: 숲 사람은 팔이 다리보다 훨씬 길어 땅을 걷기보다 나무 사이를 흔들며 건너가요. 밤마다 나뭇가지를 꺾어 새 잠자리를 엮어요.
column2: The forest man's arms are far longer than his legs, so he swings between trees rather than walking on the ground. Every night he breaks branches and weaves a new bed.

column1: 삽에는 통나무 하나를 배 모양으로 파서 만든 류트입니다. 같은 가락을 돌고 돌며 튕겨 춤추는 이의 발걸음을 이끕니다.
column2: The sape is a lute carved from a single log in the shape of a boat. Its plucked melody goes round and round, leading the dancers' steps.

column1: 삽에는 통나무 하나를 배 모양으로 파서 만든 류트예요. 같은 가락을 돌고 돌며 튕겨 춤추는 이의 발걸음을 이끌어요.
column2: The sape is a lute carved from a single log in the shape of a boat. Its plucked melody goes round and round, leading the dancers' steps.

column1: 긴 집 하나에 수십 가족이 한 지붕 아래 삽니다. 손님은 긴 툇마루에서 재우니 먼저 집주인에게 소금이나 칼을 선물하면 좋겠습니다.
column2: Dozens of families live under one roof in a single longhouse. Guests sleep on the long veranda, so a gift of salt or a knife to the master of the house first would be good.

column1: 긴 집 하나에 수십 가족이 한 지붕 아래 살아요. 손님은 긴 툇마루에서 재우니 먼저 집주인에게 소금이나 칼을 선물하면 좋겠어요.
column2: Dozens of families live under one roof in a single longhouse. Guests sleep on the long veranda, so a gift of salt or a knife to the master of the house first would be good.

column1: 다야크 사람들은 코뿔새를 하늘 신의 새로 여겨, 그 깃털을 들고 춤추며 날갯짓을 흉내 냅니다. 숲 사람을 해치면 숲의 넋이 노한다고 믿습니다.
column2: The Dayak hold the hornbill to be the bird of the sky god, and dance holding its feathers, mimicking its wingbeats. They believe harming the forest people angers the spirit of the forest.

column1: 다야크 사람들은 코뿔새를 하늘 신의 새로 여겨, 그 깃털을 들고 춤추며 날갯짓을 흉내 내요. 숲 사람을 해치면 숲의 넋이 노한다고 믿어요.
column2: The Dayak hold the hornbill to be the bird of the sky god, and dance holding its feathers, mimicking its wingbeats. They believe harming the forest people angers the spirit of the forest.

column1: 이다키는 숨을 볼에 모았다 내보내며 쉬지 않고 붑니다. 숨 쉬는 틈이 들리지 않아 땅이 우는 듯한 낮은 소리가 끝없이 이어집니다.
column2: The yidaki is played without pause, gathering breath in the cheeks and pushing it out. You can't hear the breathing gaps, so a low sound like the earth groaning goes on and on.

column1: 이다키는 숨을 볼에 모았다 내보내며 쉬지 않고 불어요. 숨 쉬는 틈이 들리지 않아 땅이 우는 듯한 낮은 소리가 끝없이 이어져요.
column2: The yidaki is played without pause, gathering breath in the cheeks and pushing it out. You can't hear the breathing gaps, so a low sound like the earth groaning goes on and on.

column1: 꿈의 시대에 조상들이 걸으며 노래해 땅과 물길을 만들었다고 믿습니다. 그 노래 길을 외우면 바위와 샘 하나하나의 이름을 압니다.
column2: They believe that in the Dreaming, the ancestors made the land and the waterways by walking and singing. Memorize those song paths and you know the name of every rock and spring.

column1: 꿈의 시대에 조상들이 걸으며 노래해 땅과 물길을 만들었다고 믿어요. 그 노래 길을 외우면 바위와 샘 하나하나의 이름을 알아요.
column2: They believe that in the Dreaming, the ancestors made the land and the waterways by walking and singing. Memorize those song paths and you know the name of every rock and spring.

column1: 마른 철에 들불을 놓아 묵은 풀을 태우면 새 풀이 돋아 캥거루가 모입니다. 불 놓는 때와 자리를 아는 것이 이들의 농사입니다.
column2: Setting fire to the old grass in the dry season makes new grass sprout and draws the kangaroos. Knowing when and where to set fires is their farming.

column1: 마른 철에 들불을 놓아 묵은 풀을 태우면 새 풀이 돋아 캥거루가 모여요. 불 놓는 때와 자리를 아는 것이 이들의 농사예요.
column2: Setting fire to the old grass in the dry season makes new grass sprout and draws the kangaroos. Knowing when and where to set fires is their farming.

column1: 꿀개미는 배에 꿀을 가득 채워 구슬처럼 부풀어 있습니다. 머리를 잡고 배를 깨물면 단 꿀이 톡 터집니다.
column2: Honey ants swell like beads with their bellies full of honey. Hold the head and bite the belly and sweet honey bursts out.

column1: 꿀개미는 배에 꿀을 가득 채워 구슬처럼 부풀어 있어요. 머리를 잡고 배를 깨물면 단 꿀이 톡 터져요.
column2: Honey ants swell like beads with their bellies full of honey. Hold the head and bite the belly and sweet honey bursts out.

column1: 롤리 경은 가슴에 눈과 입이 달린 「에와이파노마」 사람들이 이 강 위쪽에 산다고 써서 퍼뜨렸습니다. 직접 본 사람은 아무도 없었습니다.
column2: Sir Raleigh wrote and spread the tale that the "Ewaipanoma," with eyes and mouths in their chests, lived up this river. No one ever saw them with his own eyes.

column1: 롤리 경은 가슴에 눈과 입이 달린 「에와이파노마」 사람들이 이 강 위쪽에 산다고 써서 퍼뜨렸어요. 직접 본 사람은 아무도 없었어요.
column2: Sir Raleigh wrote and spread the tale that the "Ewaipanoma," with eyes and mouths in their chests, lived up this river. No one ever saw them with his own eyes.

column1: 노래하는 이가 조롱박 딸랑이를 흔들며 머리를 어깨 사이로 깊이 묻습니다. 멀리 배에서 보면 정말 머리 없이 가슴으로 노래하는 것 같습니다.
column2: The singer shakes a gourd rattle and sinks his head deep between his shoulders. Seen from a ship far off, it really does look like someone singing from his chest with no head.

column2: The singer shakes a gourd rattle and sinks his head deep between his shoulders. Seen from a ship far off, it really does look like someone singing from his chest with no head.

column1: 모리체 야자 줄기 속을 긁어 물에 헹구고 가라앉은 하얀 가루로 납작한 빵을 굽습니다. 맛은 담담하고 쫀득합니다.
column2: They scrape the pith from moriche palm trunks, rinse it in water, and bake flat bread from the white powder that settles. The taste is mild and chewy.

column1: 모리체 야자 줄기 속을 긁어 물에 헹구고 가라앉은 하얀 가루로 납작한 빵을 구워요. 맛은 담담하고 쫀득해요.
column2: They scrape the pith from moriche palm trunks, rinse it in water, and bake flat bread from the white powder that settles. The taste is mild and chewy.

column1: 통나무 하나를 불로 지지고 파서 만든 통배인데, 어떤 것은 스무 명이 탑니다. 강어귀 갈래 물길을 이 배 없이는 다닐 수 없습니다.
column2: Dugouts are made by burning and hollowing a single log, and some carry twenty people. You can't get through the branching channels of the delta without these boats.

column1: 통나무 하나를 불로 지지고 파서 만든 통배인데, 어떤 것은 스무 명이 타요. 강어귀 갈래 물길을 이 배 없이는 다닐 수 없어요.
column2: Dugouts are made by burning and hollowing a single log, and some carry twenty people. You can't get through the branching channels of the delta without these boats.

column1: 테 북은 가죽을 씌운 큰 둥근 테를 손잡이로 들고, 북면이 아니라 테 가장자리를 막대로 아래위 번갈아 칩니다. 북 치는 이가 몸을 흔들며 노래합니다.
column2: The frame drum is a big round hoop covered with hide, held by a handle, and struck with a stick alternately top and bottom on the rim, not the skin. The drummer sways and sings.

column1: 테 북은 가죽을 씌운 큰 둥근 테를 손잡이로 들고, 북면이 아니라 테 가장자리를 막대로 아래위 번갈아 쳐요. 북 치는 이가 몸을 흔들며 노래해요.
column2: The frame drum is a big round hoop covered with hide, held by a handle, and struck with a stick alternately top and bottom on the rim, not the skin. The drummer sways and sings.

column1: 나무틀에 바다표범 가죽을 팽팽히 씌운 한 사람 배는 물이 한 방울도 들지 않습니다. 뒤집혀도 노를 저어 바로 일어난다고 합니다.
column2: The one-man boat, sealskin stretched taut over a wooden frame, lets in not a drop of water. They say even if it capsizes, a stroke of the paddle rights it.

column2: The one-man boat, sealskin stretched taut over a wooden frame, lets in not a drop of water. They say even if it capsizes, a stroke of the paddle rights it.

column1: 날고기와 날 간을 먹는 덕에 채소 없이도 괴혈병에 걸리지 않습니다. 우리 선원들도 이들처럼 날고기를 먹으면 잇몸이 덜 상할 것입니다.
column2: Thanks to eating raw meat and raw liver, they don't get scurvy even without vegetables. If our sailors ate raw meat like them, their gums would suffer less.

column1: 눈 덩이를 칼로 벽돌처럼 잘라 나선으로 쌓아 올리면 하룻밤 안에 둥근 얼음집이 섭니다. 안에서 기름등 하나만 켜도 따뜻합니다.
column2: Cut blocks of snow like bricks with a knife and stack them in a spiral, and a round snow house goes up in a single night. One oil lamp inside keeps it warm.

column1: 붉은 에이리크의 아들 레이프가 처음 닿은 뒤, 토르핀 일행은 이들과 붉은 천을 가죽과 바꾸었다고 사가에 적혀 있습니다. 소가 우는 소리에 이들이 놀라 달아났다고 합니다.
column2: The sagas say that after Leif, son of Erik the Red, first landed, Thorfinn's party traded red cloth with these people for hides. They say these people fled in fright at the bellowing of a bull.

column2: They make boats by sewing birch bark with root thread and sealing the seams with pine resin. Light enough for two people to carry on their shoulders.

column2: They make boats by sewing birch bark with root thread and sealing the seams with pine resin. Light enough for two people to carry on their shoulders.

column1: 몸에 바른 붉은 흙은 모기를 쫓을 뿐 아니라, 죽은 이의 무덤에도 뿌리는 성스러운 빛깔입니다. 붉은빛은 피와 넋을 뜻합니다.
column2: The red ochre they rub on their bodies doesn't just keep off mosquitoes — it's a sacred color they also scatter on graves. Red means blood and spirit.

column2: Their bows are short, but the arrowheads are ground sharp from stone and bone. The sagas say they drove the Vikings off by launching a big black ball on the end of a pole.

column2: Pigafetta, Magellan's chronicler, wrote that they were so tall a sailor's head barely reached their waists. They wore big hide shoes, so their footprints were especially large.

column2: Whirl the bolas overhead and throw it, and the cords wrap round the animal's legs and the stones tangle it and bring it down. They hit rheas a hundred paces off.

column2: The dancers stick feathers in their hair and walk with high steps, bobbing their heads like rheas. The drumbeat is short and clipped like a bird's gait.

column2: They sew cloaks from many guanaco-calf hides joined with sinew, fur on the inside, and paint patterns on the outside with red ochre.

column1: 과나코 새끼 가죽 여러 장을 힘줄로 이어 털이 안쪽으로 가게 망토를 짓고, 바깥 면에는 붉은 흙으로 무늬를 그려요.
column2: They sew cloaks from many guanaco-calf hides joined with sinew, fur on the inside, and paint patterns on the outside with red ochre.

column1: 가까이 가 보니 키가 사람 무릎에서 허리 사이입니다. 수천이 한 줄로 바다에서 언덕까지 길을 내며 오르내립니다.
column2: Up close, they stand between a man's knee and waist. Thousands march in a single line from the sea up to the hill, wearing a path.

column1: 가까이 가 보니 키가 사람 무릎에서 허리 사이예요. 수천이 한 줄로 바다에서 언덕까지 길을 내며 오르내려요.
column2: Up close, they stand between a man's knee and waist. Thousands march in a single line from the sea up to the hill, wearing a path.

column1: 둘이 마주 서서 고개를 숙였다가 목을 하늘로 뻗고 나팔처럼 웁니다. 짝을 찾는 노래인지, 무리 전체가 그 소리로 서로를 알아봅니다.
column2: Two face each other, bow their heads, then stretch their necks to the sky and bray like trumpets. Whether it's a courting song or not, the whole colony knows each other by that sound.

column1: 둘이 마주 서서 고개를 숙였다가 목을 하늘로 뻗고 나팔처럼 울어요. 짝을 찾는 노래인지, 무리 전체가 그 소리로 서로를 알아봐요.
column2: Two face each other, bow their heads, then stretch their necks to the sky and bray like trumpets. Whether it's a courting song or not, the whole colony knows each other by that sound.

column1: 말을 걸어도 대답 대신 고개만 갸웃거리고 바다로 미끄러져 들어갑니다. 사람이라면 얼음 대륙의 말을 따로 배워야 할 것입니다.
column2: Speak to them and instead of answering they just tilt their heads and slide into the sea. If they're people, we'd have to learn the language of the ice continent.

column1: 말을 걸어도 대답 대신 고개만 갸웃거리고 바다로 미끄러져 들어가요. 사람이라면 얼음 대륙의 말을 따로 배워야 할 거예요.
column2: Speak to them and instead of answering they just tilt their heads and slide into the sea. If they're people, we'd have to learn the language of the ice continent.

column1: 검은 옷처럼 보이던 것은 깃털이고, 팔은 노처럼 납작한 날개입니다. 물에 들면 물고기보다 빨리 헤엄칩니다.
column2: What looked like black coats are feathers, and their arms are wings flat as oars. In the water they swim faster than fish.

column1: 검은 옷처럼 보이던 것은 깃털이고, 팔은 노처럼 납작한 날개예요. 물에 들면 물고기보다 빨리 헤엄쳐요.
column2: What looked like black coats are feathers, and their arms are wings flat as oars. In the water they swim faster than fish.

column1: 서안의 비석은 당나라 때인 781년에 세웠고, 위에는 연꽃 위의 십자가가, 옆에는 시리아 글자와 한자가 함께 새겨졌습니다.
column2: The stele at Xi'an was raised in 781 under the Tang, with a cross on a lotus at the top and Syriac letters and Chinese characters carved side by side.

column1: 서안의 비석은 당나라 때인 781년에 세웠고, 위에는 연꽃 위의 십자가가, 옆에는 시리아 글자와 한자가 함께 새겨졌어요.
column2: The stele at Xi'an was raised in 781 under the Tang, with a cross on a lotus at the top and Syriac letters and Chinese characters carved side by side.

column1: 시편을 시리아 말로 두 무리가 번갈아 주고받으며 노래합니다. 가락이 길고 꺾여 서방 성가와는 다른 동방의 소리입니다.
column2: Two choirs trade the psalms back and forth in Syriac. The melodies are long and bending — an Eastern sound unlike Western chant.

column1: 시편을 시리아 말로 두 무리가 번갈아 주고받으며 노래해요. 가락이 길고 꺾여 서방 성가와는 다른 동방의 소리예요.
column2: Two choirs trade the psalms back and forth in Syriac. The melodies are long and bending — an Eastern sound unlike Western chant.

column1: 나무판을 망치로 두드리는 소리가 기도 시간을 알립니다. 노아가 방주를 지을 때 망치질로 사람들을 불렀다는 데서 왔다고 합니다.
column2: The sound of a hammer on a wooden board announces the hour of prayer. They say it comes from Noah summoning people with his hammer while building the Ark.

column1: 나무판을 망치로 두드리는 소리가 기도 시간을 알려요. 노아가 방주를 지을 때 망치질로 사람들을 불렀다는 데서 왔다고 해요.
column2: The sound of a hammer on a wooden board announces the hour of prayer. They say it comes from Noah summoning people with his hammer while building the Ark.

column1: 성찬 빵에는 해마다 묵은 반죽을 조금씩 떼어 넣는데, 이 누룩이 처음 사도들의 빵에서 이어졌다고 믿습니다. 「거룩한 누룩」이라 부릅니다.
column2: Every year a bit of the old dough is added to the communion bread, and they believe this leaven goes back to the bread of the first apostles. They call it "the Holy Leaven."

column1: 성찬 빵에는 해마다 묵은 반죽을 조금씩 떼어 넣는데, 이 누룩이 처음 사도들의 빵에서 이어졌다고 믿어요. 「거룩한 누룩」이라 불러요.
column2: Every year a bit of the old dough is added to the communion bread, and they believe this leaven goes back to the bread of the first apostles. They call it "the Holy Leaven."

column1: 마을 사람들은 흡혈귀가 집주인의 허락 없이는 문지방을 넘지 못한다고 믿습니다. 그래서 밤손님에게는 결코 「들어오라」고 말하지 않습니다.
column2: The villagers believe a vampire can't cross the threshold without the master of the house's permission. So they never say "come in" to a guest at night.

column1: 마을 사람들은 흡혈귀가 집주인의 허락 없이는 문지방을 넘지 못한다고 믿어요. 그래서 밤손님에게는 결코 「들어오라」고 말하지 않아요.
column2: The villagers believe a vampire can't cross the threshold without the master of the house's permission. So they never say "come in" to a guest at night.

column1: 바이올린 둘과 쳄발롬이 점점 빨라지면 「호라」 원이 더 크게 돌고, 칼루샤리 사내들은 방울 단 다리로 높이 차오르며 땅을 구릅니다.
column2: As the two violins and the cimbalom speed up, the "hora" circle spins wider, and the Călușari men kick high on belled legs and stamp the ground.

column1: 바이올린 둘과 쳄발롬이 점점 빨라지면 「호라」 원이 더 크게 돌고, 칼루샤리 사내들은 방울 단 다리로 높이 차오르며 땅을 굴러요.
column2: As the two violins and the cimbalom speed up, the "hora" circle spins wider, and the Călușari men kick high on belled legs and stamp the ground.

column1: 노란 옥수수 죽 「마말리가」를 실로 잘라 양젖 치즈와 크림을 얹어 먹습니다. 마늘은 반찬이자 문간의 부적입니다.
column2: They cut yellow "mămăligă" cornmeal porridge with a thread and eat it topped with sheep's cheese and cream. Garlic is both a side dish and a charm at the door.

column1: 노란 옥수수 죽 「마말리가」를 실로 잘라 양젖 치즈와 크림을 얹어 먹어요. 마늘은 반찬이자 문간의 부적이에요.
column2: They cut yellow "mămăligă" cornmeal porridge with a thread and eat it topped with sheep's cheese and cream. Garlic is both a side dish and a charm at the door.

column1: 성 주인의 소문은 꼬챙이 공이라 불린 블라드 공에게서 시작되었다고 합니다. 그는 오스만 포로 수천을 말뚝에 꽂아 세웠습니다.
column2: They say the rumors about the lord of the castle started with Prince Vlad, called the Impaler. He set thousands of Ottoman prisoners up on stakes.

column1: 성 주인의 소문은 꼬챙이 공이라 불린 블라드 공에게서 시작되었다고 해요. 그는 오스만 포로 수천을 말뚝에 꽂아 세웠어요.
column2: They say the rumors about the lord of the castle started with Prince Vlad, called the Impaler. He set thousands of Ottoman prisoners up on stakes.

column1: 테포나스틀리는 통나무 위에 H자 모양 혀 두 개를 파서, 두드리는 자리마다 높고 낮은 두 소리가 납니다. 우에우에틀은 재규어 가죽을 씌워 손바닥으로 칩니다.
column2: The teponaztli is a log with two H-shaped tongues cut into it, so each spot you strike gives a high or a low note. The huehuetl is covered with jaguar skin and struck with the palms.

column1: 테포나스틀리는 통나무 위에 H자 모양 혀 두 개를 파서, 두드리는 자리마다 높고 낮은 두 소리가 나요. 우에우에틀은 재규어 가죽을 씌워 손바닥으로 쳐요.
column2: The teponaztli is a log with two H-shaped tongues cut into it, so each spot you strike gives a high or a low note. The huehuetl is covered with jaguar skin and struck with the palms.

column1: 테노치티틀란은 호수 위 섬에 세웠고, 세 갈래 둑길이 뭍으로 뻗습니다. 집 사이로 물길이 나서 사람들이 통배로 다닙니다.
column2: Tenochtitlan was built on an island in a lake, with three causeways reaching to the shore. Canals run between the houses and people get around by dugout.

column1: 테노치티틀란은 호수 위 섬에 세웠고, 세 갈래 둑길이 뭍으로 뻗어요. 집 사이로 물길이 나서 사람들이 통배로 다녀요.
column2: Tenochtitlan was built on an island in a lake, with three causeways reaching to the shore. Canals run between the houses and people get around by dugout.

column1: 마콰우이틀은 나무칼 양쪽 날에 흑요석 조각을 촘촘히 박았습니다. 강철보다 날카로워 말 목도 한 번에 벤다고 합니다.
column2: The macuahuitl is a wooden sword with obsidian chips set close along both edges. Sharper than steel, they say it can cut a horse's neck in one stroke.

column1: 마콰우이틀은 나무칼 양쪽 날에 흑요석 조각을 촘촘히 박았어요. 강철보다 날카로워 말 목도 한 번에 벤다고 해요.
column2: The macuahuitl is a wooden sword with obsidian chips set close along both edges. Sharper than steel, they say it can cut a horse's neck in one stroke.

column1: 카카오 음료는 거품을 내려고 높이에서 다른 그릇으로 쏟아 붓습니다. 고추와 바닐라를 넣어 쓰고 매운데, 귀족과 전사만 마십니다.
column2: To raise a froth, the cacao drink is poured from a height into another vessel. With chili and vanilla it's bitter and hot — only nobles and warriors drink it.

column1: 카카오 음료는 거품을 내려고 높이에서 다른 그릇으로 쏟아 부어요. 고추와 바닐라를 넣어 쓰고 매운데, 귀족과 전사만 마셔요.
column2: To raise a froth, the cacao drink is poured from a height into another vessel. With chili and vanilla it's bitter and hot — only nobles and warriors drink it.

column1: 케나는 갈대에 구멍 여섯을 뚫고 엄지 구멍 하나를 더한 피리입니다. 바람 소리처럼 쓸쓸한 가락이 높은 고원에서 멀리 울립니다.
column2: The quena is a reed flute with six holes and a thumbhole. Its melancholy melody, like the sound of the wind, carries far across the high plateau.

column1: 케나는 갈대에 구멍 여섯을 뚫고 엄지 구멍 하나를 더한 피리예요. 바람 소리처럼 쓸쓸한 가락이 높은 고원에서 멀리 울려요.
column2: The quena is a reed flute with six holes and a thumbhole. Its melancholy melody, like the sound of the wind, carries far across the high plateau.

column1: 석벽은 모르타르 없이 돌을 깎아 맞췄는데, 이음매에 칼날 하나 들어가지 않습니다. 열두 모서리를 낸 돌도 있습니다.
column2: The stone walls are cut and fitted without mortar, and not even a knife blade fits in the joints. Some stones have twelve corners.

column1: 석벽은 모르타르 없이 돌을 깎아 맞췄는데, 이음매에 칼날 하나 들어가지 않아요. 열두 모서리를 낸 돌도 있어요.
column2: The stone walls are cut and fitted without mortar, and not even a knife blade fits in the joints. Some stones have twelve corners.

column1: 추뇨는 감자를 밤에 얼리고 낮에 밟아 물을 빼기를 며칠 되풀이해 만듭니다. 돌처럼 가벼워 몇 해를 두어도 썩지 않습니다.
column2: Chuño is made by freezing potatoes at night and treading out the water by day, over and over for days. Light as stone, it keeps for years without rotting.

column1: 추뇨는 감자를 밤에 얼리고 낮에 밟아 물을 빼기를 며칠 되풀이해 만들어요. 돌처럼 가벼워 몇 해를 두어도 썩지 않아요.
column2: Chuño is made by freezing potatoes at night and treading out the water by day, over and over for days. Light as stone, it keeps for years without rotting.

column1: 산길 곳곳에 창고와 쉼터가 있고, 파발꾼이 이어 달려 쿠스코 소식을 하루 수백 리씩 나릅니다. 군대가 다녀도 먹을 것이 떨어지지 않습니다.
column2: There are storehouses and rest stops all along the mountain roads, and relay runners carry news from Cuzco hundreds of li a day. Even an army on the march never runs out of food.

column1: 산길 곳곳에 창고와 쉼터가 있고, 파발꾼이 이어 달려 쿠스코 소식을 하루 수백 리씩 날라요. 군대가 다녀도 먹을 것이 떨어지지 않아요.
column2: There are storehouses and rest stops all along the mountain roads, and relay runners carry news from Cuzco hundreds of li a day. Even an army on the march never runs out of food.

column1: 초록 커튼 아래 끝이 붉은 술처럼 물들고, 주름이 바람에 날리듯 몇 숨 사이에 모양을 바꿉니다. 붓이 따라가지 못합니다.
column2: Beneath the green curtain the lower edge is tinged like red tassels, and the folds change shape in a few breaths as if blown by the wind. No brush can keep up.

column1: 초록 커튼 아래 끝이 붉은 술처럼 물들고, 주름이 바람에 날리듯 몇 숨 사이에 모양을 바꿔요. 붓이 따라가지 못해요.
column2: Beneath the green curtain the lower edge is tinged like red tassels, and the folds change shape in a few breaths as if blown by the wind. No brush can keep up.

column1: 사미 사람들은 이 빛이 죽은 이의 넋이라 여겨, 빛 아래서 휘파람을 불거나 손가락질하지 않습니다. 조용히 요이크 노래만 읊조립니다.
column2: The Sámi believe these lights are the souls of the dead, so they never whistle or point beneath them. They only hum their joik songs quietly.

column1: 사미 사람들은 이 빛이 죽은 이의 넋이라 여겨, 빛 아래서 휘파람을 불거나 손가락질하지 않아요. 조용히 요이크 노래만 읊조려요.
column2: The Sámi believe these lights are the souls of the dead, so they never whistle or point beneath them. They only hum their joik songs quietly.

column1: 빛이 가장 짙은 쪽은 늘 북쪽 하늘입니다. 별이 가려진 밤에도 이 빛이 걸린 쪽으로 대략 방위를 잡을 수 있습니다.
column2: The lights are always thickest in the northern sky. Even on nights when the stars are hidden, you can take a rough bearing from where they hang.

column1: 빛이 가장 짙은 쪽은 늘 북쪽 하늘이에요. 별이 가려진 밤에도 이 빛이 걸린 쪽으로 대략 방위를 잡을 수 있어요.
column2: The lights are always thickest in the northern sky. Even on nights when the stars are hidden, you can take a rough bearing from where they hang.

column1: 빛이 일렁이는 밤에는 나침반 바늘이 조금씩 떨리며 흔들립니다. 하늘의 이 불과 땅의 자석이 무슨 끈으로 이어진 듯합니다.
column2: On nights the lights ripple, the compass needle trembles and wavers a little. It's as if this fire in the sky and the lodestone of the earth are joined by some cord.

column1: 빛이 일렁이는 밤에는 나침반 바늘이 조금씩 떨리며 흔들려요. 하늘의 이 불과 땅의 자석이 무슨 끈으로 이어진 듯해요.
column2: On nights the lights ripple, the compass needle trembles and wavers a little. It's as if this fire in the sky and the lodestone of the earth are joined by some cord.

column1: 캘리컷 시장에서 산 값의 스무 배 넘게 리스본에서 받습니다. 배 한 척 후추로 항해 비용 전부를 갚고도 남습니다.
column2: It fetches more than twenty times the Calicut market price in Lisbon. One shipload of pepper pays the whole voyage's costs with plenty left over.

column1: 캘리컷 시장에서 산 값의 스무 배 넘게 리스본에서 받아요. 배 한 척 후추로 항해 비용 전부를 갚고도 남아요.
column2: It fetches more than twenty times the Calicut market price in Lisbon. One shipload of pepper pays the whole voyage's costs with plenty left over.

column1: 덜 익은 초록 열매를 따서 햇볕에 말리면 껍질이 쪼그라들며 검게 됩니다. 갈아 뿌리면 소금에 절인 고기의 묵은내가 가십니다.
column2: Pick the green berries unripe and dry them in the sun, and the skins shrivel and turn black. Grind and sprinkle it and the stale smell of salt meat is gone.

column1: 덜 익은 초록 열매를 따서 햇볕에 말리면 껍질이 쪼그라들며 검게 돼요. 갈아 뿌리면 소금에 절인 고기의 묵은내가 가셔요.
column2: Pick the green berries unripe and dry them in the sun, and the skins shrivel and turn black. Grind and sprinkle it and the stale smell of salt meat is gone.

column1: 열매가 덩굴에 포도송이처럼 길게 매달려 큰 나무를 감고 오릅니다. 비가 많은 말라바르 언덕에서만 이렇게 잘 자랍니다.
column2: The berries hang long on the vine like bunches of grapes, and the vine climbs and wraps big trees. It only grows this well on the rainy hills of Malabar.

column1: 열매가 덩굴에 포도송이처럼 길게 매달려 큰 나무를 감고 올라요. 비가 많은 말라바르 언덕에서만 이렇게 잘 자라요.
column2: The berries hang long on the vine like bunches of grapes, and the vine climbs and wraps big trees. It only grows this well on the rainy hills of Malabar.

column2: Split the apricot-like fruit and a red, net-like husk wraps the seed. The seed is nutmeg; the red husk becomes a different spice called mace.

column2: Peel the outer bark of young shoots, shave the inner bark thin and dry it, and it curls up on its own. Small quills are nested inside bigger ones to make sticks.

column2: Ceylon's is paper-thin and sweet, gentler in scent than the cassia bark of the southern seas. It's lovely warmed in wine.

column2: Portugal built a fortress at Colombo to get this bark from the king of Ceylon. They say only the Salagama people are allowed to peel it.

column2: When seasickness turns your stomach, chew a piece and it settles. Brewed, it warms the body and drives off a cold too.

column2: Candied in honey it keeps long, and the English grind it into powder for bread and cakes. Half-dried root is hotter and more fragrant.

column2: It doesn't rot even shipped as live roots, so it's easy to replant in other lands. That's why it's far cheaper than pepper.

column2: Bite one berry and you taste clove, cinnamon and nutmeg all at once. That's why the English call it "allspice."

column2: Green beans smell only grassy, but roast them brown in a pan and a nutty aroma bursts out. Grind, boil in water, let the grounds settle, and drink from the top.

column2: Since the water must be boiled, people who drink these leaves get fewer bellyaches. It clears the head and keeps sleep away.

column2: In the Aztec markets, a hundred of these beans buy a turkey, three an avocado. There are even fakes going round — hollowed out and filled with clay.

column2: The long yellow pods grow straight from the trunk, not the branches. It only thrives in the shade of big trees.

column2: The physicians of Seville sell this leaf as medicine for headaches and wounds. But sailors who get a taste for it can't quit and live with a cough.

column1: 부리가 매처럼 굽은 매부리바다거북의 등딱지에서만 이런 두꺼운 판이 나옵니다. 산호초에서 해면을 뜯어 먹고 삽니다.
column2: Only the shell of the hawksbill turtle, with its hooked, hawk-like beak, gives plates this thick. It lives on coral reefs grazing on sponges.

column1: 부리가 매처럼 굽은 매부리바다거북의 등딱지에서만 이런 두꺼운 판이 나와요. 산호초에서 해면을 뜯어 먹고 살아요.
column2: Only the shell of the hawksbill turtle, with its hooked, hawk-like beak, gives plates this thick. It lives on coral reefs grazing on sponges.

column1: 인삼 뿌리는 사람 모양일수록 약효가 크다고 합니다. 기운이 빠진 병자에게 달여 먹이면 맥이 다시 섭니다.
column2: They say the more a ginseng root looks like a person, the stronger its effect. Brew it for a sick man whose strength has drained and his pulse rallies.

column1: 인삼 뿌리는 사람 모양일수록 약효가 크다고 해요. 기운이 빠진 병자에게 달여 먹이면 맥이 다시 서요.
column2: They say the more a ginseng root looks like a person, the stronger its effect. Brew it for a sick man whose strength has drained and his pulse rallies.

column1: 감초는 씹으면 설탕보다 단맛이 오래 남습니다. 동방 의원들은 쓴 약 대부분에 이것을 조금씩 넣어 맛을 맞춥니다.
column2: Chew licorice and the sweetness lingers longer than sugar. Eastern physicians add a little to most bitter medicines to balance the taste.

column1: 감초는 씹으면 설탕보다 단맛이 오래 남아요. 동방 의원들은 쓴 약 대부분에 이것을 조금씩 넣어 맛을 맞춰요.
column2: Chew licorice and the sweetness lingers longer than sugar. Eastern physicians add a little to most bitter medicines to balance the taste.

column1: 조선 산삼은 같은 무게의 은보다 비싸 왜인과 청나라 상인이 앞다투어 삽니다. 습기를 먹으면 곰팡이가 피니 바람 잘 드는 상자에 실어야 합니다.
column2: Joseon wild ginseng is dearer than its weight in silver, and Japanese and Qing merchants scramble to buy it. It molds if it gets damp, so ship it in well-aired boxes.

column1: 조선 산삼은 같은 무게의 은보다 비싸 왜인과 청나라 상인이 앞다투어 사요. 습기를 먹으면 곰팡이가 피니 바람 잘 드는 상자에 실어야 해요.
column2: Joseon wild ginseng is dearer than its weight in silver, and Japanese and Qing merchants scramble to buy it. It molds if it gets damp, so ship it in well-aired boxes.

column1: 껍질이 노랗게 익으면 날로 먹고, 초록일 때는 굽거나 쪄서 감자처럼 먹습니다. 잎은 넓어 음식을 싸서 찌는 데 씁니다.
column2: When the skin ripens yellow it's eaten raw; while green it's roasted or steamed and eaten like potatoes. The broad leaves are used to wrap food for steaming.

column1: 껍질이 노랗게 익으면 날로 먹고, 초록일 때는 굽거나 쪄서 감자처럼 먹어요. 잎은 넓어 음식을 싸서 찌는 데 써요.
column2: When the skin ripens yellow it's eaten raw; while green it's roasted or steamed and eaten like potatoes. The broad leaves are used to wrap food for steaming.

column1: 익기 전 초록 송이째 매달아 두면 며칠씩 차례로 익어 갑니다. 한 송이에 백 개 넘게 달려 선원 여럿이 며칠 먹습니다.
column2: Hang the bunch whole while still green and it ripens bit by bit over several days. One bunch holds over a hundred, enough for several sailors for days.

column1: 익기 전 초록 송이째 매달아 두면 며칠씩 차례로 익어 가요. 한 송이에 백 개 넘게 달려 선원 여럿이 며칠 먹어요.
column2: Hang the bunch whole while still green and it ripens bit by bit over several days. One bunch holds over a hundred, enough for several sailors for days.

column1: 나무처럼 보여도 줄기는 잎집이 겹겹이 말린 것이라 칼 한 번에 베입니다. 열매를 맺고 나면 그 줄기는 죽고 옆에서 새 싹이 올라옵니다.
column2: It looks like a tree, but the trunk is just leaf sheaths rolled layer on layer — one stroke of a knife cuts it. Once it fruits that stalk dies, and a new shoot comes up beside it.

column1: 나무처럼 보여도 줄기는 잎집이 겹겹이 말린 것이라 칼 한 번에 베여요. 열매를 맺고 나면 그 줄기는 죽고 옆에서 새 싹이 올라와요.
column2: It looks like a tree, but the trunk is just leaf sheaths rolled layer on layer — one stroke of a knife cuts it. Once it fruits that stalk dies, and a new shoot comes up beside it.

column1: 숯불 재 속에 묻어 두면 껍질이 터지며 꿀 같은 진이 흘러나옵니다. 밤보다 달고 속이 노랗습니다.
column2: Bury it in the coals and ash and the skin bursts and honey-like syrup oozes out. Sweeter than chestnuts, and yellow inside.

column1: 숯불 재 속에 묻어 두면 껍질이 터지며 꿀 같은 진이 흘러나와요. 밤보다 달고 속이 노래요.
column2: Bury it in the coals and ash and the skin bursts and honey-like syrup oozes out. Sweeter than chestnuts, and yellow inside.

column1: 덩굴 한 마디만 잘라 꽂아도 뿌리를 내려 모래땅에서도 자랍니다. 섬에 머물 때 심어 두면 석 달 뒤에 캘 수 있습니다.
column2: Cut just one node of the vine and stick it in the ground and it roots, growing even in sandy soil. Plant some while we stay on an island and in three months you can dig them up.

column1: 덩굴 한 마디만 잘라 꽂아도 뿌리를 내려 모래땅에서도 자라요. 섬에 머물 때 심어 두면 석 달 뒤에 캘 수 있어요.
column2: Cut just one node of the vine and stick it in the ground and it roots, growing even in sandy soil. Plant some while we stay on an island and in three months you can dig them up.

column1: 루손에서 이 덩굴을 몰래 새끼줄 속에 꼬아 넣어 푸젠으로 가져간 상인이 있었다고 합니다. 그 뒤 흉년마다 이것이 사람들을 살렸습니다.
column2: They say a merchant smuggled this vine from Luzon to Fujian by twisting it into a straw rope. After that, it saved people in every famine.

column1: 루손에서 이 덩굴을 몰래 새끼줄 속에 꼬아 넣어 푸젠으로 가져간 상인이 있었다고 해요. 그 뒤 흉년마다 이것이 사람들을 살렸어요.
column2: They say a merchant smuggled this vine from Luzon to Fujian by twisting it into a straw rope. After that, it saved people in every famine.

column1: 상관 지하 감옥 벽에는 손톱으로 긁은 자국이 남아 있습니다. 이곳에서 배를 기다리다 죽은 사람들의 이름은 어디에도 적혀 있지 않습니다.
column2: The walls of the trading post's dungeon still bear marks scratched with fingernails. The names of those who died here waiting for the ships are written nowhere.

column1: 상관 지하 감옥 벽에는 손톱으로 긁은 자국이 남아 있어요. 이곳에서 배를 기다리다 죽은 사람들의 이름은 어디에도 적혀 있지 않아요.
column2: The walls of the trading post's dungeon still bear marks scratched with fingernails. The names of those who died here waiting for the ships are written nowhere.

column1: 노예선 밑창에는 사람들이 몸을 펴지도 못하게 빽빽이 눕혀집니다. 대서양을 건너는 동안 이질과 굶주림으로 대여섯에 하나꼴로 숨진다고 합니다.
column2: In the holds of slave ships people are laid so tightly they can't even stretch out. They say one in five or six dies of dysentery and hunger during the Atlantic crossing.

column1: 노예선 밑창에는 사람들이 몸을 펴지도 못하게 빽빽이 눕혀져요. 대서양을 건너는 동안 이질과 굶주림으로 대여섯에 하나꼴로 숨진다고 해요.
column2: In the holds of slave ships people are laid so tightly they can't even stretch out. They say one in five or six dies of dysentery and hunger during the Atlantic crossing.

column1: 세례를 준다며 사람을 사고파는 일을 정당하다 말하는 이들이 있습니다. 그러나 사람을 쇠사슬에 묶는 일을 축복할 신은 없습니다.
column2: Some say buying and selling people is justified because they're baptized. But there is no god who would bless putting people in chains.

column1: 세례를 준다며 사람을 사고파는 일을 정당하다 말하는 이들이 있어요. 그러나 사람을 쇠사슬에 묶는 일을 축복할 신은 없어요.
column2: Some say buying and selling people is justified because they're baptized. But there is no god who would bless putting people in chains.

column1: 붙잡힌 사람들은 서로 다른 말을 써서 옆 사람과도 이야기를 나누지 못합니다. 그들의 고향 이름이라도 받아 적어 두어야겠습니다.
column2: The captives speak different languages, so they can't even talk to the person beside them. I should at least write down the names of their homelands.

column1: 붙잡힌 사람들은 서로 다른 말을 써서 옆 사람과도 이야기를 나누지 못해요. 그들의 고향 이름이라도 받아 적어 두어야겠어요.
column2: The captives speak different languages, so they can't even talk to the person beside them. I should at least write down the names of their homelands.

column1: 벽돌 기단이 계단처럼 층층이 물러나며 쌓였고, 층마다 흙을 담았던 칸이 남아 있습니다. 강 쪽에서 보면 정말 언덕이 공중에 걸린 듯했을 겁니다.
column2: The brick terraces step back tier upon tier, and each tier still has the compartments that held soil. From the river it really must have looked like a hill hanging in midair.

column1: 벽돌 기단이 계단처럼 층층이 물러나며 쌓였고, 층마다 흙을 담았던 칸이 남아 있어요. 강 쪽에서 보면 정말 언덕이 공중에 걸린 듯했을 거예요.
column2: The brick terraces step back tier upon tier, and each tier still has the compartments that held soil. From the river it really must have looked like a hill hanging in midair.

column1: 벽돌 사이마다 검은 역청을 바르고 갈대 깔개와 납판을 덮어 물이 아래로 새지 않게 했습니다. 이천 년이 지났는데도 역청이 끈적합니다.
column2: Black bitumen was spread between every brick, then covered with reed mats and lead sheets so water wouldn't leak below. Two thousand years later the bitumen is still sticky.

column1: 벽돌 사이마다 검은 역청을 바르고 갈대 깔개와 납판을 덮어 물이 아래로 새지 않게 했어요. 이천 년이 지났는데도 역청이 끈적해요.
column2: Black bitumen was spread between every brick, then covered with reed mats and lead sheets so water wouldn't leak below. Two thousand years later the bitumen is still sticky.

column1: 네부카드네자르 왕이 산 많은 메디아에서 온 왕비가 고향을 그리워하자 이 정원을 지었다고 합니다. 세상의 일곱 기적 가운데 하나로 꼽혔습니다.
column2: They say King Nebuchadnezzar built this garden for his queen from mountainous Media, who longed for home. It was counted among the Seven Wonders of the World.

column1: 네부카드네자르 왕이 산 많은 메디아에서 온 왕비가 고향을 그리워하자 이 정원을 지었다고 해요. 세상의 일곱 기적 가운데 하나로 꼽혔어요.
column2: They say King Nebuchadnezzar built this garden for his queen from mountainous Media, who longed for home. It was counted among the Seven Wonders of the World.

column1: 돌로 짠 우물 셋이 나란히 뚫려 있습니다. 두레박을 사슬에 줄줄이 매달아 바퀴로 돌리며 유프라테스 물을 꼭대기까지 퍼 올렸을 것입니다.
column2: Three stone-lined wells are sunk side by side. They must have hung buckets in a row on a chain and turned a wheel to lift Euphrates water all the way to the top.

column1: 돌로 짠 우물 셋이 나란히 뚫려 있어요. 두레박을 사슬에 줄줄이 매달아 바퀴로 돌리며 유프라테스 물을 꼭대기까지 퍼 올렸을 거예요.
column2: Three stone-lined wells are sunk side by side. They must have hung buckets in a row on a chain and turned a wheel to lift Euphrates water all the way to the top.

column1: 불을 지른 자는 헤로스트라토스라 합니다. 에페소스 사람들은 그 이름을 입에 올리지 못하게 법으로 막았지만 이름은 오히려 남았습니다.
column2: They say the man who set the fire was Herostratus. The Ephesians passed a law forbidding anyone to speak his name, yet the name survived all the same.

column1: 불을 지른 자는 헤로스트라토스라 해요. 에페소스 사람들은 그 이름을 입에 올리지 못하게 법으로 막았지만 이름은 오히려 남았어요.
column2: They say the man who set the fire was Herostratus. The Ephesians passed a law forbidding anyone to speak his name, yet the name survived all the same.

column1: 남은 기둥 하나를 재어 보니 돛대 셋을 이은 높이입니다. 이런 기둥이 백스물일곱 개였다면 신전 길이는 배 열 척을 늘어세운 것과 맞먹습니다.
column2: Measuring the one column left standing, it's the height of three masts end to end. If there were a hundred and twenty-seven of these, the temple was as long as ten ships in a row.

column1: 남은 기둥 하나를 재어 보니 돛대 셋을 이은 높이예요. 이런 기둥이 백스물일곱 개였다면 신전 길이는 배 열 척을 늘어세운 것과 맞먹어요.
column2: Measuring the one column left standing, it's the height of three masts end to end. If there were a hundred and twenty-seven of these, the temple was as long as ten ships in a row.

column1: 이곳의 아르테미스는 가슴에 알 같은 것을 주렁주렁 단 풍요의 여신이었습니다. 사도 바울이 이 도시에서 은으로 만든 여신의 사당을 팔던 장인들과 다투었습니다.
column2: The Artemis here was a fertility goddess hung with egg-like things on her chest. The Apostle Paul clashed in this city with the craftsmen who sold silver shrines of the goddess.

column1: 이곳의 아르테미스는 가슴에 알 같은 것을 주렁주렁 단 풍요의 여신이었어요. 사도 바울이 이 도시에서 은으로 만든 여신의 사당을 팔던 장인들과 다투었어요.
column2: The Artemis here was a fertility goddess hung with egg-like things on her chest. The Apostle Paul clashed in this city with the craftsmen who sold silver shrines of the goddess.

column1: 들판이 늪이 되어 발목까지 빠집니다. 모기가 많으니 밤에는 언덕 위 마을로 올라가 묵는 편이 낫습니다.
column2: The plain has turned to marsh and you sink to your ankles. There are lots of mosquitoes, so better to go up and stay in the village on the hill at night.

column1: 들판이 늪이 되어 발목까지 빠져요. 모기가 많으니 밤에는 언덕 위 마을로 올라가 묵는 편이 나아요.
column2: The plain has turned to marsh and you sink to your ankles. There are lots of mosquitoes, so better to go up and stay in the village on the hill at night.

column1: 거상은 데메트리오스 왕의 포위를 견딘 기념으로, 적이 버리고 간 공성 무기를 팔아 세웠다고 합니다. 서 있던 것은 겨우 쉰여섯 해였습니다.
column2: They say the colossus was raised to celebrate surviving King Demetrius's siege, paid for by selling the siege engines the enemy left behind. It stood only fifty-six years.

column1: 거상은 데메트리오스 왕의 포위를 견딘 기념으로, 적이 버리고 간 공성 무기를 팔아 세웠다고 해요. 서 있던 것은 겨우 쉰여섯 해였어요.
column2: They say the colossus was raised to celebrate surviving King Demetrius's siege, paid for by selling the siege engines the enemy left behind. It stood only fifty-six years.

column1: 항구 어귀가 좁아 두 다리를 벌린 거상 사이로 배가 지나갔다는 이야기가 있습니다. 하지만 물살과 바닥을 보면 한쪽 둑 위에 서 있었다고 보는 편이 맞습니다.
column2: There's a tale that the harbor mouth was so narrow ships passed between the colossus's spread legs. But judging by the currents and the seabed, it more likely stood on one of the moles.

column1: 항구 어귀가 좁아 두 다리를 벌린 거상 사이로 배가 지나갔다는 이야기가 있어요. 하지만 물살과 바닥을 보면 한쪽 둑 위에 서 있었다고 보는 편이 맞아요.
column2: There's a tale that the harbor mouth was so narrow ships passed between the colossus's spread legs. But judging by the currents and the seabed, it more likely stood on one of the moles.

column1: 낙타 구백 마리 짐이면 청동이 수백 톤입니다. 녹여서 대포로 부으면 함대 하나를 무장시킬 양이었습니다.
column2: Nine hundred camel-loads means hundreds of tons of bronze. Melted down and cast into cannon, it would have armed a whole fleet.

column1: 낙타 구백 마리 짐이면 청동이 수백 톤이에요. 녹여서 대포로 부으면 함대 하나를 무장시킬 양이었어요.
column2: Nine hundred camel-loads means hundreds of tons of bronze. Melted down and cast into cannon, it would have armed a whole fleet.

column1: 기사단 성벽은 대포를 맞도록 두껍고 낮게 고쳐 쌓았습니다. 투르크 군이 몇 달을 쏘아도 버틴 까닭이 보입니다.
column2: The Knights' walls were rebuilt thick and low to take cannon fire. You can see why they held out for months under Turkish guns.

column1: 기사단 성벽은 대포를 맞도록 두껍고 낮게 고쳐 쌓았어요. 투르크 군이 몇 달을 쏘아도 버틴 까닭이 보여요.
column2: The Knights' walls were rebuilt thick and low to take cannon fire. You can see why they held out for months under Turkish guns.

column1: 등대는 프톨레마이오스 왕 때 소스트라토스가 지었습니다. 건축가는 왕의 이름을 회반죽에 쓰고 그 아래 돌에 제 이름을 새겨, 회반죽이 떨어지자 제 이름이 드러났다고 합니다.
column2: The lighthouse was built by Sostratus under King Ptolemy. They say the architect wrote the king's name in plaster and carved his own in the stone beneath, so when the plaster fell, his name appeared.

column2: This coast is low and flat, so the land can't be seen from the sea. That's why they guided ships with fire by night and smoke by day.

column1: 네모난 아래층, 팔각 가운데층, 둥근 꼭대기층의 세 단이었다고 합니다. 요새 아래 깔린 돌의 크기로 보아 높이가 대성당 첨탑의 세 배는 됐겠습니다.
column2: They say it had three tiers: a square bottom, an octagonal middle and a round top. Judging by the stones beneath the fortress, it must have been three times as tall as a cathedral spire.

column2: It's said a great mirror at the top gathered sunlight and sent the light far out. There's even a tale they set enemy ships on fire with the mirror.

column2: Books seized in the harbor were tagged "from the ships." They say Athens even lent its original tragedies and never got them back, losing the deposit.

column2: The scholar Eratosthenes measured the earth's circumference here by comparing the shadows of rods in two cities. His figure nearly matches today's charts.

column2: The scrolls were made by layering strips of Nile papyrus crosswise and pounding them. They were weak against damp, so they had to be recopied once a century.

column2: They say when Mausolus died, Artemisia — his sister and wife — mixed his ashes in wine and drank them. The word "mausoleum" comes from this king's name.

column2: The lion carvings set into the castle walls are alive down to every hair of their manes. They say four Greek sculptors each took one side of the tomb and competed in skill.

column2: The base alone is more than thirty paces a side. Above it rose a colonnade, a stepped roof, and at the very top a chariot drawn by four horses.

column2: Every four years people from all over Greece gathered here to compete in running and wrestling. They say even wars stopped during that time.

column2: One drum of a fallen column is as wide as two cartwheels stacked. The saying that the seated Zeus would have burst through the roof if he stood up is no exaggeration.

column2: The outer circuit is more than five hundred paces. With eighty numbered entrances, fifty thousand people could come and go in no time.

column2: Beneath the arena floor you can see the tunnels for animal cages and lifting frames. A gladiator stood on the sand never knowing where a lion would burst out.

column2: King Piye of Kush raised his army here and conquered Egypt. Afterwards the black pharaohs ruled the whole Nile for a time.

column2: The Egyptians saw the cobra-shaped peak as the sacred serpent on a crown. So they believed this mountain was the home of the god Amun.

column2: The pyramids here are much smaller than Egypt's and steeper. A little over ten paces at the base, with tips like needles.

column2: Beside the tower are marked the spots where the Buddha stayed and walked for a week each after his enlightenment. Pilgrims walk that path barefoot.

column2: The bodhi leaf ends in a long, tail-like tip so rainwater drips off easily. The stems are long, so the leaves always flutter even without wind.

column2: They say King Ashoka first built a shrine here. The kings of Burma rebuilt the fallen tower many times.

column2: The Tang monk Xuanzang studied here five years and went home loaded with scriptures. They say to get in, you first had to pass the gatekeeper monk's questions.

column2: There are more than ten brick buildings lined with monks' cells. Each room still has a stone bed and a niche for a lamp.

column2: The bricks are scorched dark red, and some have melted like glass and fused together. The saying that it burned for three months is no idle talk.

column2: On the gateway pillars, yakshis hang from tree branches, their bodies curved. The Buddha is never shown in human form — only by footprints and empty seats.

column2: West of the mound are holes where log posts once stood in a circle. They seem to have counted the seasons by lining up the sunrise with the posts.

column2: The islanders say the god Maui brought these stones in his canoe. In fact, they say the eleventh Tuʻi Tonga king raised it.

column2: Coral stone is soft when freshly cut but hardens in the air. That's how they could carve and fit blocks this big.

column2: Each of the pyramid's four stairways has ninety-one steps, and with the one at the top that makes three hundred sixty-five. The days of the year, built in stone.

column1: 계단 앞에서 손뼉을 치면 메아리가 새가 우는 소리처럼 꺾여 돌아옵니다. 깃털 달린 새 케찰의 울음을 흉내 냈다고 합니다.
column2: Clap your hands in front of the stairs and the echo comes back bent like a birdcall. They say it imitates the cry of the quetzal.

column2: The sacred well is a round pit of water ringed by sheer walls. In droughts, they say, gold, jade and even people were thrown in for the rain god Chaac.

column1: 공놀이 마당 벽에는 진 편 우두머리의 목을 베는 장면이 새겨져 있습니다. 목에서 피 대신 뱀이 솟아 나옵니다.
column2: The walls of the ball court show the captain of the losing side being beheaded. Serpents rise from his neck instead of blood.

column2: The rose window on the west front is nearly ten paces across, with the labors of the twelve months and the zodiac in colored glass around the Virgin at the center. At sunset the inside of the cathedral glows red.

column1: 바깥에서 벽을 받치는 날아가는 버팀벽 덕에 벽을 얇게 하고 창을 크게 낼 수 있었습니다. 지붕의 괴물 석상은 입으로 빗물을 뱉어 내는 홈통입니다.
column2: Thanks to the flying buttresses propping the walls from outside, the walls could be thin and the windows large. The gargoyles on the roof are drainpipes that spit rainwater from their mouths.

column1: 남쪽 탑의 큰 종 에마뉘엘이 울리면 센 강 건너까지 배 밑이 떨립니다. 이 성당 성가대에서 여러 성부가 함께 부르는 노래가 처음 나왔다고 합니다.
column2: When Emmanuel, the great bell of the south tower, rings, boat bottoms tremble across the Seine. They say singing in many parts together began in this cathedral's choir.

column2: When Emmanuel, the great bell of the south tower, rings, boat bottoms tremble across the Seine. They say singing in many parts together began in this cathedral's choir.

column1: 성 루이 왕이 비싼 값에 사들인 그리스도의 가시관이 이곳에 모셔져 있습니다. 해마다 성금요일에 사람들에게 내보입니다.
column2: The Crown of Thorns, bought at great price by King Saint Louis, is kept here. It's shown to the people every Good Friday.

column2: Seated, it's as tall as two masts end to end, and a single thumb is the size of a small child's body. It's hollow, so you can go inside.

column2: The bronze couldn't be poured in one go, so it was cast in more than thirty pours and joined. The seams remain as horizontal lines across the body.

column2: They say it was gilded at first, but wind and rain stripped it all, and now it's covered in green patina. Only a little gold remains beside the cheek.

column2: The palm sticks poking out of the mud walls are footholds for climbing up when the walls are replastered every year. After the rains, the whole town turns out to plaster.

column2: Here, books brought by camel from North Africa are a better trade than salt or gold. Every scholarly family keeps books in chests and hands them down for generations.

column2: The scholars here welcome you warmly if you open in Arabic. It's the custom here to first put a question of law to a guest.

column2: The southern shrine belongs to Huitzilopochtli, god of war; the northern to Tlaloc, god of rain. Even the shrine roofs are painted apart, red and blue.

column2: Every time a new king took the throne, the Aztecs covered the old pyramid whole and built a bigger one over it. They say there are seven layers inside, like an onion.

column2: Beat the great snakeskin drum at the top and it's heard in the villages across the lake. On festival days the conch trumpets sound all day long.

column2: Coral was cut from the sea, dried in the sun and dressed. The lime was made by burning coral, so the whole mosque came out of the sea.

column2: All the gold coming down from Sofala passed through this port. The sultan here was rich enough to mint his own copper coins.

column2: Blue-patterned celadon bowls are set into every round recess of the ceiling, twinkling when the light hits them. It's as if the trade route stretching all the way to China hangs on the wall.

column2: The Malwiya tower's spiral ramp winds five times around as it climbs. It's as tall as five masts end to end, but there's no railing, so you can't climb it on windy days.

column2: This mosque, built by Caliph al-Mutawakkil, was once the largest in the Islamic world. They say the caliph rode a donkey all the way to the top of the tower.

column2: It's built of fired brick bonded with bitumen. Some forty round towers stand at even intervals along the enclosure wall.

column2: Bramante drew the first plans, and now the aged Michelangelo is in charge of the dome. Decades after the first stone was laid, there's still no end in sight.

column2: Two young princes were locked in this tower and vanished. King Henry's queen Anne Boleyn was beheaded in the tower courtyard too.

column2: Two young princes were locked in this tower and vanished. King Henry's queen Anne Boleyn was beheaded in the tower courtyard too.

column1: 흰 돌은 바다 건너 노르망디 캉에서 실어 온 석회암입니다. 벽 두께가 아래층은 다섯 걸음 가까이 됩니다.
column2: The white stone is limestone shipped across the sea from Caen in Normandy. The walls on the ground floor are nearly five paces thick.

column2: The white stone is limestone shipped across the sea from Caen in Normandy. The walls on the ground floor are nearly five paces thick.

column1: 왕의 동물원에는 사자와 표범, 북극곰까지 있습니다. 북극곰은 줄에 묶인 채 템스 강에 들어가 물고기를 잡는다고 합니다.
column2: The king's menagerie has lions, leopards, even a polar bear. They say the polar bear goes into the Thames on a chain to catch fish.

column2: The king's menagerie has lions, leopards, even a polar bear. They say the polar bear goes into the Thames on a chain to catch fish.

column1: 탑 안 무기고에 갑옷과 창이 산처럼 쌓여 있고, 화약도 이곳에 둡니다. 강가 쪽 성벽에 대포가 줄지어 템스를 겨눕니다.
column2: Armor and spears are piled like mountains in the tower's armory, and the gunpowder is kept here too. Cannons line the riverside walls, trained on the Thames.

column1: 검은 옻칠 바탕에 금으로 라마야나 이야기를 그린 벽이 등잔 빛에 번쩍입니다. 뒷벽 생명의 나무는 분홍·초록 유리 조각을 모자이크로 박았습니다.
column2: Walls painted in gold on black lacquer with the Ramayana gleam in the lamplight. The tree of life on the back wall is a mosaic of pink and green glass pieces.

column2: Walls painted in gold on black lacquer with the Ramayana gleam in the lamplight. The tree of life on the back wall is a mosaic of pink and green glass pieces.

column1: 두 강이 만나는 곶에 서 있어 메콩을 오르내리는 배가 모두 이 절 앞을 지납니다. 건기에는 강바닥 바위가 드러나 물길을 잘 골라야 합니다.
column2: It stands on the point where two rivers meet, so every boat going up or down the Mekong passes before this temple. In the dry season rocks show in the riverbed — pick your channel carefully.

column1: 두 강이 만나는 곶에 서 있어 메콩을 오르내리는 배가 모두 이 절 앞을 지나요. 건기에는 강바닥 바위가 드러나 물길을 잘 골라야 해요.
column2: It stands on the point where two rivers meet, so every boat going up or down the Mekong passes before this temple. In the dry season rocks show in the riverbed — pick your channel carefully.

column1: 이 절에서 라오 왕이 대관식을 올립니다. 왕의 장례 수레도 이 절에 모셔져 있습니다.
column2: The Lao kings are crowned at this temple. The king's funeral carriage is kept here too.

column1: 이 절에서 라오 왕이 대관식을 올려요. 왕의 장례 수레도 이 절에 모셔져 있어요.
column2: The Lao kings are crowned at this temple. The king's funeral carriage is kept here too.

column1: 아스키아 무함마드는 메카에 가면서 금 삼십만 냥을 가져가 순례자들에게 나누었다고 합니다. 돌아올 때 이집트에서 흙과 나무를 실어 와 이 무덤을 쌓았습니다.
column2: They say Askia Muhammad took three hundred thousand pieces of gold on his way to Mecca and gave them out to pilgrims. On his return he brought earth and timber from Egypt and built this tomb.

column1: 아스키아 무함마드는 메카에 가면서 금 삼십만 냥을 가져가 순례자들에게 나누었다고 해요. 돌아올 때 이집트에서 흙과 나무를 실어 와 이 무덤을 쌓았어요.
column2: They say Askia Muhammad took three hundred thousand pieces of gold on his way to Mecca and gave them out to pilgrims. On his return he brought earth and timber from Egypt and built this tomb.

column1: 흙 피라미드는 계단처럼 층을 지어 돛대 두 개 높이로 솟았습니다. 위에 오르면 니제르 강이 굽이도는 것이 보입니다.
column2: The earthen pyramid rises in steps to the height of two masts. From the top you can see the Niger winding along.

column1: 흙 피라미드는 계단처럼 층을 지어 돛대 두 개 높이로 솟았어요. 위에 오르면 니제르 강이 굽이도는 것이 보여요.
column2: The earthen pyramid rises in steps to the height of two masts. From the top you can see the Niger winding along.

column1: 튀어나온 막대는 아카시아 나무입니다. 흙이 우기에 씻겨 내리면 그 막대를 디디고 올라가 다시 바릅니다.
column2: The jutting sticks are acacia wood. When the rains wash the mud down, they climb up on those sticks and plaster it again.

column1: 튀어나온 막대는 아카시아 나무예요. 흙이 우기에 씻겨 내리면 그 막대를 디디고 올라가 다시 발라요.
column2: The jutting sticks are acacia wood. When the rains wash the mud down, they climb up on those sticks and plaster it again.

column1: 파리 대학에서 쫓겨 온 영국 학자들이 모여 이 도시가 커졌다고 합니다. 학생과 시민이 싸워 수십 명이 죽은 일도 있었습니다.
column2: They say this town grew when English scholars driven out of the University of Paris gathered here. There was even a brawl between students and townsfolk in which dozens died.

column1: 파리 대학에서 쫓겨 온 영국 학자들이 모여 이 도시가 커졌다고 해요. 학생과 시민이 싸워 수십 명이 죽은 일도 있었어요.
column2: They say this town grew when English scholars driven out of the University of Paris gathered here. There was even a brawl between students and townsfolk in which dozens died.

column1: 여기서는 논쟁 시합에서 라틴어 삼단논법으로 상대를 몰아붙여야 학위를 받습니다. 길에서 학생에게 말을 걸면 대뜸 라틴어로 답합니다.
column2: Here you only get your degree by pinning your opponent with Latin syllogisms in a disputation. Speak to a student in the street and he'll answer straight away in Latin.

column1: 여기서는 논쟁 시합에서 라틴어 삼단논법으로 상대를 몰아붙여야 학위를 받아요. 길에서 학생에게 말을 걸면 대뜸 라틴어로 답해요.
column2: Here you only get your degree by pinning your opponent with Latin syllogisms in a disputation. Speak to a student in the street and he'll answer straight away in Latin.

column1: 신학부 강당 천장은 돌 갈빗대가 그물처럼 얽히고 매듭마다 문장과 머리글자가 새겨져 있습니다. 그런 매듭이 사백 개가 넘습니다.
column2: The ceiling of the Divinity School is a net of stone ribs, with coats of arms and initials carved at every boss. There are more than four hundred such bosses.

column1: 신학부 강당 천장은 돌 갈빗대가 그물처럼 얽히고 매듭마다 문장과 머리글자가 새겨져 있어요. 그런 매듭이 사백 개가 넘어요.
column2: The ceiling of the Divinity School is a net of stone ribs, with coats of arms and initials carved at every boss. There are more than four hundred such bosses.

column1: 부처의 두 눈 사이 코 자리에는 물음표처럼 굽은 선이 그려져 있습니다. 네팔 숫자 하나로, 하나 됨을 뜻한다고 합니다.
column2: Between the Buddha's two eyes, where the nose would be, is a line curled like a question mark. It's a Nepali numeral one, meaning oneness, they say.

column1: 부처의 두 눈 사이 코 자리에는 물음표처럼 굽은 선이 그려져 있어요. 네팔 숫자 하나로, 하나 됨을 뜻한다고 해요.

column1: 탑 꼭대기에서 다섯 빛깔 깃발 줄이 사방으로 늘어져 있습니다. 바람이 깃발에 적힌 기도를 하늘로 실어 간다고 믿습니다.
column2: Strings of five-colored flags hang from the top of the stupa in every direction. They believe the wind carries the prayers written on the flags up to heaven.

column1: 탑 꼭대기에서 다섯 빛깔 깃발 줄이 사방으로 늘어져 있어요. 바람이 깃발에 적힌 기도를 하늘로 실어 간다고 믿어요.
column2: Strings of five-colored flags hang from the top of the stupa in every direction. They believe the wind carries the prayers written on the flags up to heaven.

column1: 순례자들이 기도 바퀴를 돌릴 때마다 놋쇠가 덜그럭거리고 「옴 마니 반메 훔」 소리가 웅얼웅얼 섞입니다. 해 질 녘엔 긴 나팔 소리가 깔립니다.
column2: Every time pilgrims spin the prayer wheels the brass clatters, mixed with murmurs of "Om mani padme hum." At dusk the long horns drone beneath it all.

column1: 순례자들이 기도 바퀴를 돌릴 때마다 놋쇠가 덜그럭거리고 「옴 마니 반메 훔」 소리가 웅얼웅얼 섞여요. 해 질 녘엔 긴 나팔 소리가 깔려요.
column2: Every time pilgrims spin the prayer wheels the brass clatters, mixed with murmurs of "Om mani padme hum." At dusk the long horns drone beneath it all.

column1: 티베트에서 넘어온 상인들이 탑 둘레에 머물며 소금과 털을 쌀과 바꿉니다. 카트만두 장삿길의 길목입니다.
column2: Merchants who came over from Tibet stay around the stupa, trading salt and wool for rice. It's the crossroads of the Kathmandu trade route.

column2: Merchants who came over from Tibet stay around the stupa, trading salt and wool for rice. It's the crossroads of the Kathmandu trade route.

column1: 흰 코끼리는 왕이 고른 것이 아니라 스스로 산을 올랐습니다. 사람들은 부처의 사리가 자리를 고른 것이라 믿습니다.
column2: The white elephant wasn't chosen by the king — it climbed the mountain on its own. People believe it was the Buddha's relic that chose the spot.

column2: The white elephant wasn't chosen by the king — it climbed the mountain on its own. People believe it was the Buddha's relic that chose the spot.

column1: 계단은 삼백 칸이 넘고 꼭대기에서 치앙마이 성의 네모난 해자가 내려다보입니다. 산 아래보다 바람이 서늘합니다.
column2: There are more than three hundred steps, and from the top you can look down on the square moat of Chiang Mai. The wind is cooler than at the foot of the mountain.

column1: 계단은 삼백 칸이 넘고 꼭대기에서 치앙마이 성의 네모난 해자가 내려다보여요. 산 아래보다 바람이 서늘해요.
column2: There are more than three hundred steps, and from the top you can look down on the square moat of Chiang Mai. The wind is cooler than at the foot of the mountain.

column1: 계단 난간은 일곱 머리 뱀 나가의 몸이 길게 이어진 것입니다. 초록·금빛 비늘 타일이 햇빛을 받아 물결처럼 번득입니다.
column2: The stair railings are the long bodies of the seven-headed naga serpent. Green and gold scale tiles flash like waves in the sunlight.

column1: 계단 난간은 일곱 머리 뱀 나가의 몸이 길게 이어진 거예요. 초록·금빛 비늘 타일이 햇빛을 받아 물결처럼 번득여요.
column2: The stair railings are the long bodies of the seven-headed naga serpent. Green and gold scale tiles flash like waves in the sunlight.

column1: 남쪽 오문에서 북쪽 신무문까지 한 줄로 궁전이 늘어서 있고 길이가 이 리 가깝습니다. 해자 폭이 배 세 척을 나란히 띄울 만합니다.
column2: From the Meridian Gate in the south to the Gate of Divine Prowess in the north, the palaces stand in a single line nearly two li long. The moat is wide enough to float three boats side by side.

column2: From the Meridian Gate in the south to the Gate of Divine Prowess in the north, the palaces stand in a single line nearly two li long. The moat is wide enough to float three boats side by side.

column1: 영락제가 남경에서 도읍을 옮기며 열네 해에 걸쳐 지었습니다. 백만 명이 일했다고 합니다.
column2: The Yongle Emperor built it over fourteen years when he moved the capital from Nanjing. They say a million people worked on it.

column2: The Yongle Emperor built it over fourteen years when he moved the capital from Nanjing. They say a million people worked on it.

column1: 큰 기둥은 운남과 사천 깊은 산의 녹나무를 강물에 띄워 몇 해에 걸쳐 실어 왔습니다. 바닥에 깐 벽돌은 두드리면 쇠 소리가 나서 금벽돌이라 부릅니다.
column2: The great columns are nanmu wood from deep in the mountains of Yunnan and Sichuan, floated down the rivers over several years. The floor bricks ring like metal when tapped, so they're called gold bricks.

column1: 큰 기둥은 운남과 사천 깊은 산의 녹나무를 강물에 띄워 몇 해에 걸쳐 실어 왔어요. 바닥에 깐 벽돌은 두드리면 쇠 소리가 나서 금벽돌이라 불러요.
column2: The great columns are nanmu wood from deep in the mountains of Yunnan and Sichuan, floated down the rivers over several years. The floor bricks ring like metal when tapped, so they're called gold bricks.

column1: 누런 기와는 황제만 쓸 수 있는 빛깔입니다. 처마 끝에 줄지어 앉은 작은 짐승 상의 수로 건물의 격을 알 수 있습니다.
column2: Yellow roof tiles are a color only the emperor may use. You can tell a building's rank by the number of little beast figures sitting in a row along the eave ends.

column2: Yellow roof tiles are a color only the emperor may use. You can tell a building's rank by the number of little beast figures sitting in a row along the eave ends.

column1: 양파 지붕 아홉 개가 저마다 다른 무늬입니다. 하나는 비늘, 하나는 나선, 하나는 다이아몬드라 그리려면 한 개씩 따로 봐야 합니다.
column2: Each of the nine onion domes has a different pattern — one scales, one spirals, one diamonds — so to draw them you have to study each one separately.

column1: 양파 지붕 아홉 개가 저마다 다른 무늬예요. 하나는 비늘, 하나는 나선, 하나는 다이아몬드라 그리려면 한 개씩 따로 봐야 해요.
column2: Each of the nine onion domes has a different pattern — one scales, one spirals, one diamonds — so to draw them you have to study each one separately.

column1: 카잔은 성모 보호 축일에 무너졌습니다. 그래서 본래 이름은 성모 보호 대성당이고, 뒤에 거룩한 바보 바실리를 묻은 예배당 이름이 붙었습니다.
column2: Kazan fell on the Feast of the Intercession. So its original name is the Cathedral of the Intercession, and later it took the name of the chapel where Basil the Holy Fool was buried.

column1: 카잔은 성모 보호 축일에 무너졌어요. 그래서 본래 이름은 성모 보호 대성당이고, 뒤에 거룩한 바보 바실리를 묻은 예배당 이름이 붙었어요.
column2: Kazan fell on the Feast of the Intercession. So its original name is the Cathedral of the Intercession, and later it took the name of the chapel where Basil the Holy Fool was buried.

column1: 가운데 높은 탑 둘레에 여덟 개의 예배당이 별 모양으로 둘러섰습니다. 안은 좁은 복도가 미로처럼 이어집니다.
column2: Eight chapels stand around the tall central tower in a star shape. Inside, narrow corridors wind like a maze.

column1: 가운데 높은 탑 둘레에 여덟 개의 예배당이 별 모양으로 둘러섰어요. 안은 좁은 복도가 미로처럼 이어져요.
column2: Eight chapels stand around the tall central tower in a star shape. Inside, narrow corridors wind like a maze.

column1: 성벽 위의 제비 꼬리 모양 톱니는 밀라노 성을 본뜬 것입니다. 붉은 벽돌을 굽는 가마를 이탈리아 장인들이 따로 세웠다고 합니다.
column2: The swallowtail merlons on top of the walls copy the castle at Milan. They say Italian masters built separate kilns to fire the red bricks.

column1: 성벽 위의 제비 꼬리 모양 톱니는 밀라노 성을 본뜬 거예요. 붉은 벽돌을 굽는 가마를 이탈리아 장인들이 따로 세웠다고 해요.
column2: The swallowtail merlons on top of the walls copy the castle at Milan. They say Italian masters built separate kilns to fire the red bricks.

column1: 성벽은 세모꼴로 둘러 있고 망루가 스무 개입니다. 둘레를 걸으면 한 시진 가까이 걸립니다.
column2: The walls run round in a triangle with twenty towers. Walking the circuit takes close to two hours.

column2: The tsars are crowned in the Cathedral of the Dormition. Five golden domes hold up their crosses.

column2: In the courtyard sits a huge bronze cannon with a barrel more than five paces long. The cannonballs are as big as a man, but they say it's never once been fired.

column2: Wooden shops crowd the edges of the square, selling furs, salt, honey and wax. The tsar's officials collect rent from every shop.

column2: The round stone platform where decrees are read was also used as a scaffold. Rebels had their heads cut off in this square.

column1: 탑 서쪽 벽 아래에 코뿔소 머리가 튀어나와 있습니다. 인도에서 마누엘 왕에게 보낸 코뿔소를 본떴다고 합니다.
column2: A rhinoceros head juts out beneath the tower's west wall. They say it's modeled on the rhinoceros sent from India to King Manuel.

column2: Past the tower, the Tagus widens and runs out to sea. Here you wait for both wind and ebb tide before weighing anchor.

column1: 난간과 창틀에 돌로 깎은 밧줄 매듭과 그물, 혼천의가 얽혀 있습니다. 뱃사람의 물건을 돌에 새기는 것이 마누엘 왕 시절의 멋입니다.
column2: Stone-carved rope knots, nets and armillary spheres twine around the balustrades and window frames. Carving sailors' gear in stone was the fashion of King Manuel's day.

column2: The lower battery sits right at the waterline, so it can fire straight into the side of an incoming ship. When the tide rises, the storeroom below becomes a prison.

column2: As the hull is towed along the canal, the warehouses on both sides hand out masts, oars, rope and cannon in turn. That's how they fit out a whole ship in a single day.

column2: As the hull is towed along the canal, the warehouses on both sides hand out masts, oars, rope and cannon in turn. That's how they fit out a whole ship in a single day.

column1: 밧줄 공방은 지붕 덮인 긴 복도가 몇 백 걸음이나 이어집니다. 삼 가닥을 꼬면서 뒷걸음질로 걸어가 한 줄을 만듭니다.
column2: The ropewalk is a covered corridor several hundred paces long. They twist the hemp strands while walking backwards to make a single line.

column1: 밧줄 공방은 지붕 덮인 긴 복도가 몇 백 걸음이나 이어져요. 삼 가닥을 꼬면서 뒷걸음질로 걸어가 한 줄을 만들어요.
column2: The ropewalk is a covered corridor several hundred paces long. They twist the hemp strands while walking backwards to make a single line.

column1: 단테도 이 조선소에서 겨울에 역청을 끓이는 모습을 보고 지옥의 펄펄 끓는 늪을 썼습니다. 입구 사자 하나의 어깨에는 바이킹의 룬 글자가 새겨져 있습니다.
column2: Dante saw them boiling pitch in this shipyard in winter and wrote of the seething marsh of hell. One of the lions at the entrance has Viking runes carved on its shoulder.

column2: The Padrón Real is constantly updated from the logs handed in by returning pilots. Secretly copy it and pass it to foreigners and it costs you your life.

column2: All the gold and silver from the New World is weighed here and the king's fifth is taken off. Silver not entered in the ledger is contraband.

column2: Amerigo Vespucci was the first chief pilot here. Pilots must pass an examination here before they can sail on New World ships.

column2: In the middle of the ceiling, the fingers of God and Adam almost touch, and not quite. The whole painting's breath gathers in that hand's-breadth gap.

column2: Each day's portion had to be painted before the wet plaster dried. Look at the ceiling and the boundaries of each day's plaster show like a patchwork quilt.

column2: The conclave of cardinals that elects a new pope is held inside this chapel. White smoke from the burned ballots means a pope has been chosen.

column2: They say the chapel's length, width and height follow exactly the dimensions of Solomon's Temple given in the Bible. The length is three times the width.

column2: Botticelli's painting of Venus rising from the sea on a seashell is here. The wind god puffs his cheeks and scatters petals.

column2: Vasari built it on Grand Duke Cosimo's orders. The name Uffizi means "offices" in Italian.

column2: The secret corridor runs over the roofs of the bridge across the Arno all the way to the Pitti Palace. The Grand Duke had the butchers on the bridge replaced by goldsmiths because of the smell.

column2: Drop a plumb line from the top and it lands a man's height outside the base. Eight stories, about two and a half masts tall.

column2: The ground is soft river clay and sand, so the south side sank more. There's a tale that Galileo dropped a heavy ball and a light ball together from this tower.

column2: The seven bells at the top each have a different note, making a whole scale. Because the tower leans, the heaviest bell isn't rung anymore.

column2: The playhouse is a wooden frame of more than twenty sides with a thatched roof. When the company quarreled with the landlord, they pulled down their old theater and carried the timber across the river to build this one.

column2: Standing in the yard costs a penny, a bench under the roof two pence, and with a cushion three. The money goes into clay boxes at the door that are smashed open and counted later.

column2: They use real gunpowder for cannon sounds in the middle of plays. They say a spark once caught the thatch and the whole theater burned down.

column2: When the actors bore them, the groundlings throw hazelnut shells and jeer. The players here have voices that can blast their lines through the racket.

column2: The walls run nearly ten li around, with star-shaped bastions jutting out at every corner. French engineers helped, mixing in Western methods of fortification.

column2: The walls run nearly ten li around, with star-shaped bastions jutting out at every corner. French engineers helped, mixing in Western methods of fortification.

column1: 황성은 흐엉 강 건너 응우 산을 앞에 두고 앉았습니다. 그 산이 황제를 가리는 병풍 노릇을 한다고 풍수에서 말합니다.
column2: The imperial city faces Ngự Bình mountain across the Perfume River. Geomancers say that mountain serves as a screen shielding the emperor.

column1: 오문 위 다섯 지붕 누각은 누런 기와와 초록 기와를 번갈아 얹었습니다. 처마 끝마다 용이 꼬리를 말아 올렸습니다.
column2: The five-roofed pavilion over the Noon Gate alternates yellow and green tiles. A dragon curls its tail up at every eave end.

column1: 해협 가운데로는 대서양 물이 지중해로 쉼 없이 들어오고, 밑바닥으로는 짠물이 거꾸로 빠져나갑니다. 동풍 레반테가 불면 바위 꼭대기에 구름 깃발이 걸립니다.
column2: Through the middle of the strait Atlantic water pours endlessly into the Mediterranean, while along the bottom salt water flows back out. When the east wind, the Levanter, blows, a banner of cloud hangs on the top of the Rock.

column1: 이름은 무어인 장수 타리크가 이 바위에 올라 에스파냐로 쳐들어간 데서 왔습니다. 「자발 타리크」, 곧 타리크의 산입니다.
column2: The name comes from the Moorish commander Tariq, who landed on this rock and invaded Spain. "Jabal Tariq" — Tariq's mountain.

column1: 바위 원숭이는 이 땅의 다른 어디에도 살지 않고 바다 건너 아프리카 산에만 삽니다. 원숭이가 떠나면 이 바위의 주인이 바뀐다는 말이 있습니다.
column2: The rock apes live nowhere else on this continent — only in the mountains of Africa across the sea. They say if the apes leave, the Rock will change hands.

column1: 석회암을 파고 들어가면 해협 전체를 대포 사정거리에 넣을 수 있습니다. 이 바위를 쥔 자가 지중해의 문을 쥐는 셈입니다.
column2: Tunnel into the limestone and the whole strait comes within cannon range. Whoever holds this rock holds the gate of the Mediterranean.

column1: 석회암을 파고 들어가면 해협 전체를 대포 사정거리에 넣을 수 있어요. 이 바위를 쥔 자가 지중해의 문을 쥐는 셈이에요.

column1: 소 플리니우스가 맞은편 미세노에서 그날을 보고 편지로 남겼습니다. 소나무처럼 위로 솟았다가 옆으로 퍼지는 검은 구름이었다고 합니다.
column2: Pliny the Younger saw that day from Misenum across the bay and left an account in a letter. He said it was a black cloud that shot up like a pine tree, then spread out sideways.

column2: Pliny the Younger saw that day from Misenum across the bay and left an account in a letter. He said it was a black cloud that shot up like a pine tree, then spread out sideways.

column1: 바깥 쌍봉 가운데 하나는 옛 큰 산의 테두리이고 그 안에서 새 원뿔이 자랐습니다. 꼭대기 김에서 유황 냄새가 나니 땅속 불은 아직 살아 있습니다.
column2: Of the twin outer peaks, one is the rim of the old great mountain, and a new cone has grown inside it. The steam at the top smells of sulfur, so the fire underground is still alive.

column1: 화산재 흙에서 자란 포도로 담근 술을 「그리스도의 눈물」이라 부릅니다. 맛이 맑고 끝에 쌉쌀한 돌 내음이 납니다.
column2: The wine made from grapes grown in volcanic-ash soil is called "Tears of Christ." It tastes clean, with a bitter, stony note at the end.

column1: 화산재 흙에서 자란 포도로 담근 술을 「그리스도의 눈물」이라 불러요. 맛이 맑고 끝에 쌉쌀한 돌 내음이 나요.
column2: The wine made from grapes grown in volcanic-ash soil is called "Tears of Christ." It tastes clean, with a bitter, stony note at the end.

column1: 비탈의 우물물이 마르거나 땅에서 김이 솟으면 곧 터진다는 징조입니다. 그런 날엔 배를 바다 쪽에 대 두는 것이 좋습니다.
column2: When the wells on the slopes run dry or steam rises from the ground, it's a sign an eruption is near. On such days it's best to keep the ships on the seaward side.

column1: 능선 네 개 사이 벽면이 거의 깎아지른 듯해 눈이 쌓이지 못하고 검은 바위가 드러납니다. 높이는 사천오백 미터에 가깝습니다.
column2: The faces between its four ridges are nearly sheer, so snow can't settle and black rock shows. It's close to four thousand five hundred meters high.

column1: 골짜기 마을 체르마트 사람들은 이 봉우리에 귀신이 산다며 오르지 않습니다. 오르려면 이른 새벽에 떠나 해가 바위를 녹여 돌이 떨어지기 전에 내려와야 합니다.
column2: The people of Zermatt in the valley say demons live on this peak and won't climb it. To climb, you have to leave before dawn and come down before the sun thaws the rock and stones start falling.

column2: The people of Zermatt in the valley say demons live on this peak and won't climb it. To climb, you have to leave before dawn and come down before the sun thaws the rock and stones start falling.

column1: 구름 깃발은 늘 바람 아래쪽으로 날립니다. 그리려면 해 뜰 때 봉우리 끝만 붉게 물드는 순간을 잡아야 합니다.
column2: The cloud banner always streams downwind. To paint it, catch the moment at sunrise when only the tip of the peak glows red.

column2: The cloud banner always streams downwind. To paint it, catch the moment at sunrise when only the tip of the peak glows red.

column1: 이 산은 페룬의 산이라고도 불립니다. 여름 오후면 정말 봉우리에 천둥 구름이 몰려와 번개가 칩니다.
column2: This mountain is also called Perun's mountain. On summer afternoons, thunderclouds really do gather on the peak and lightning strikes.

column1: 이 산은 페룬의 산이라고도 불려요. 여름 오후면 정말 봉우리에 천둥 구름이 몰려와 번개가 쳐요.
column2: This mountain is also called Perun's mountain. On summer afternoons, thunderclouds really do gather on the peak and lightning strikes.

column1: 흰 바위는 대리석이라 빗물에 녹아 구멍과 골이 많습니다. 기슭의 바이쿠셰프 소나무는 줄기가 사람 셋이 안을 만큼 굵습니다.
column2: The white rock is marble, so rain dissolves it into pits and gullies. The Baikushev pine at its foot has a trunk so thick it takes three men to hug it.

column1: 봉우리 북쪽은 깎아지른 벼랑이고 남쪽은 완만한 비탈입니다. 남쪽으로 오르면 하루면 꼭대기에 섭니다.
column2: The north side of the peak is a sheer cliff and the south a gentle slope. Climb from the south and you can stand on the summit in a day.

column2: The north side of the peak is a sheer cliff and the south a gentle slope. Climb from the south and you can stand on the summit in a day.

column1: 위 계단은 낮고 넓게, 아래 계단은 높게 떨어집니다. 두 단을 합치면 서른 미터 남짓이고, 협곡은 폭포에서 비스듬히 꺾여 나갑니다.
column2: The upper step is low and wide, the lower one a high drop. Together the two tiers fall about thirty meters, and the gorge bends away at an angle from the falls.

column1: 물빛이 흰 것은 빙하가 깎아 낸 고운 돌가루가 섞였기 때문입니다. 흐비타라는 강 이름도 흰 강이라는 뜻입니다.
column2: The water is white because it carries fine rock flour ground by the glacier. The river's name, Hvítá, means "white river" too.

column1: 협곡 속으로 물이 떨어져 소리가 땅 밑에서 울리듯 둔하게 퍼집니다. 가까이 가면 옆 사람 말소리가 들리지 않습니다.
column2: The water drops into the gorge, so the sound spreads dull, as if rumbling from underground. Get close and you can't hear the person next to you.

column2: The water drops into the gorge, so the sound spreads dull, as if rumbling from underground. Get close and you can't hear the person next to you.

column1: 얼음 밑에서 불이 터지면 녹은 물이 한꺼번에 쏟아지는 빙하 홍수가 납니다. 이 섬 사람들은 그것을 「얼음 달리기」라 부릅니다.
column2: When fire erupts under the ice, the melted water pours out all at once in a glacial flood. The islanders call it "jökulhlaup," the glacier run.

column1: 얼음 밑에서 불이 터지면 녹은 물이 한꺼번에 쏟아지는 빙하 홍수가 나요. 이 섬 사람들은 그것을 「얼음 달리기」라 불러요.
column2: When fire erupts under the ice, the melted water pours out all at once in a glacial flood. The islanders call it "jökulhlaup," the glacier run.

column1: 빙모 남쪽 기슭 농가들은 홍수 물길을 피해 높은 둔덕에 지었습니다. 화산재가 내리면 양을 우리 안에 들이고 풀을 덮어야 합니다.
column2: The farms on the southern slopes of the ice cap are built on high mounds, out of the flood paths. When ash falls, bring the sheep into the pens and cover the hay.

column2: The farms on the southern slopes of the ice cap are built on high mounds, out of the flood paths. When ash falls, bring the sheep into the pens and cover the hay.

column1: 셀랴란즈 폭포는 절벽에서 떨어지는 물 뒤로 걸어 들어갈 수 있습니다. 안에서 보면 해 지는 바다가 물 커튼 너머로 번집니다.
column2: At Seljalandsfoss you can walk in behind the water falling from the cliff. From inside, the sunset sea blurs beyond the curtain of water.

column1: 이 산은 남쪽 바다에서 배를 몰 때 좋은 표지입니다. 흰 빙모가 보이면 뭍이 가깝고, 그 아래 해안은 모래톱이라 배를 대면 안 됩니다.
column2: This mountain is a good landmark when sailing the southern sea. When the white ice cap is in sight, land is near — and the coast beneath is sandbar, so don't put in there.

column1: 이 산은 남쪽 바다에서 배를 몰 때 좋은 표지예요. 흰 빙모가 보이면 뭍이 가깝고, 그 아래 해안은 모래톱이라 배를 대면 안 돼요.
column2: This mountain is a good landmark when sailing the southern sea. When the white ice cap is in sight, land is near — and the coast beneath is sandbar, so don't put in there.

column1: 수도원 마당의 떨기나무는 모세가 본 바로 그 나무의 뿌리에서 자랐다고 믿습니다. 다른 데 옮겨 심으면 자라지 않는다고 합니다.
column2: They believe the bush in the monastery courtyard grew from the roots of the very bush Moses saw. They say if you transplant it anywhere else, it won't grow.

column2: They believe the bush in the monastery courtyard grew from the roots of the very bush Moses saw. They say if you transplant it anywhere else, it won't grow.

column1: 유스티니아누스 황제가 이 수도원을 성채처럼 두른 담으로 지었습니다. 무함마드가 이 수도원을 보호하겠다고 약속한 문서도 전한다고 합니다.
column2: Emperor Justinian built this monastery surrounded by walls like a fortress. They say a document in which Muhammad promised to protect this monastery has come down too.

column2: Emperor Justinian built this monastery surrounded by walls like a fortress. They say a document in which Muhammad promised to protect this monastery has come down too.

column1: 밤에 오르면 서늘하지만 꼭대기는 새벽에 얼음이 얼 만큼 춥습니다. 낙타를 모는 베두인을 길잡이로 삼으면 계단 아래 길까지 태워 줍니다.
column2: Climbing at night is cool, but the summit is cold enough to freeze by dawn. Take a camel-driving Bedouin as guide and he'll carry you as far as the foot of the steps.

column1: 밤에 오르면 서늘하지만 꼭대기는 새벽에 얼음이 얼 만큼 추워요. 낙타를 모는 베두인을 길잡이로 삼으면 계단 아래 길까지 태워 줘요.
