column2: Skulls have had faces remodeled in plaster with seashells set in the eye sockets. They kept their dead ancestors' faces alive.

column1: 엘리사의 샘이라 부르는 큰 샘이 솟아 이 사막 가운데서도 종려나무와 밭이 푸릅니다. 물을 넉넉히 받을 수 있습니다.
column2: A great spring called Elisha's Spring wells up, so even in the middle of this desert the palms and fields are green. You can get plenty of water.

column1: 엘리사의 샘이라 부르는 큰 샘이 솟아 이 사막 가운데서도 종려나무와 밭이 푸르러요. 물을 넉넉히 받을 수 있어요.
column2: A great spring called Elisha's Spring wells up, so even in the middle of this desert the palms and fields are green. You can get plenty of water.

column2: The outermost wall is a hundred sixty meters across. From the ground it looks like just piles of stone — you have to climb a high hill to see the round shape.

column2: The cliff cave entrances are narrow and high, reached only by descending ropes or climbing up.

column2: There's not a single well over the hundred kilometers from here to Abu Simbel. We must load plenty of water and fodder for the camels.

column2: A cup-shaped hollow is cut into one of the pillars. Perhaps they poured water there as an offering to the spring's god.

column2: They say a king on his way to the shrine of the goddess Nanda Devi brought dancing women along and angered the goddess. Even now the pilgrim procession passes by this lake.

column2: Over hunters chasing bison are painted soldiers on horseback, and over them elephants — thousands of years of pictures layered on one rock.

column2: Over hunters chasing bison are painted soldiers on horseback, and over them elephants — thousands of years of pictures layered on one rock.

column1: 버섯처럼 솟은 사암 바위가 수백 개이고, 그 아래 그늘마다 그림이 있습니다. 비를 피하기에 알맞은 처마입니다.
column2: There are hundreds of sandstone rocks jutting like mushrooms, and pictures in the shade under each. Eaves just right for keeping off the rain.

column2: There are hundreds of sandstone rocks jutting like mushrooms, and pictures in the shade under each. Eaves just right for keeping off the rain.

column1: 손을 잡고 둥글게 춤추는 사람들과 북을 치는 사람이 그려져 있습니다. 북소리에 맞춘 춤이었을 것입니다.
column2: There are paintings of people dancing in a circle holding hands and a man beating a drum. It must have been a dance to the drumbeat.

column2: There are paintings of people dancing in a circle holding hands and a man beating a drum. It must have been a dance to the drumbeat.

column1: 고장 사람들은 판다바 형제 가운데 힘센 비마가 숲에서 떠돌던 때 이 바위에 앉아 쉬었다고 합니다.
column2: The locals say the mighty Bhima of the Pandava brothers sat and rested on this rock when he wandered the forest.

column2: The locals say the mighty Bhima of the Pandava brothers sat and rested on this rock when he wandered the forest.

column2: Rows of water tanks are cut from the rock, and two streams were dammed with stone to bring rainwater into the city. They collect a whole year's rain.

column1: 성이 안쪽 성, 가운데 성, 아래 성 세 겹으로 나뉘고, 그 사이에 큰 마당이 있습니다. 둘레에 소금밭이 끝없이 펼쳐집니다.
column2: The city is divided into three tiers — citadel, middle town and lower town — with a great open ground between. Salt flats spread endlessly all around.

column1: 북쪽 성문 곁에 흰 돌을 박은 큰 글자 열 자가 엎어져 있습니다. 성문 위에 걸었던 이름판일 것입니다.
column2: Beside the north gate, ten large signs inlaid with white stone lie face-down. Probably a name board that hung above the city gate.

column1: 도장에 새긴 외뿔 짐승과 글자가 아주 작고 정교합니다. 조개껍데기와 마노 구슬도 이 성에서 만들었습니다.
column2: The unicorn beasts and script carved on the seals are tiny and precise. Shell and agate beads were made in this city too.

column2: The unicorn beasts and script carved on the seals are tiny and precise. Shell and agate beads were made in this city too.

column1: 화강암 벽을 거울처럼 갈아, 등불을 대면 불꽃이 벽 속에 하나 더 비칩니다. 돌가루와 모래로 몇 해를 문질렀을 겁니다.
column2: The granite walls are polished like mirrors, so hold up a lamp and another flame appears inside the wall. They must have rubbed for years with stone powder and sand.

column1: 손뼉을 한 번 치니 소리가 둥근 천장을 돌며 한참 동안 웅웅 울립니다. 승려들이 이 울림 속에서 경을 외웠을 것입니다.
column2: Clap once and the sound circles the domed ceiling, humming for a long time. Monks must have chanted scriptures inside this resonance.

column2: According to the old letters carved at the entrance, King Ashoka and his grandson gave these caves to ascetics called the Ajivikas.

column2: According to the old letters carved at the entrance, King Ashoka and his grandson gave these caves to ascetics called the Ajivikas.

column2: At the entrance of the Lomas Rishi cave, beneath an arch modeled on the eaves of a wooden house, elephants walk in a line toward a stupa.

column2: At the entrance of the Lomas Rishi cave, beneath an arch modeled on the eaves of a wooden house, elephants walk in a line toward a stupa.

column1: 세 얼굴 거상은 가운데가 고요하고, 왼쪽은 콧수염을 단 성난 얼굴, 오른쪽은 연꽃을 든 부드러운 얼굴입니다.
column2: The three-faced colossus is serene in the middle, an angry mustached face on the left, and a gentle face holding a lotus on the right.

column2: The three-faced colossus is serene in the middle, an angry mustached face on the left, and a gentle face holding a lotus on the right.

column1: 세 얼굴만으로 높이가 사람 셋을 쌓은 것보다 큽니다. 언덕 바위를 통째로 파 들어가 큰 기둥 수십 개를 남겼습니다.
column2: The three faces alone are taller than three men stacked. They cut into the hill's rock whole, leaving dozens of great pillars.

column1: 시바가 만들고 지키고 부수는 세 얼굴을 한 몸에 지녔다는 믿음을 돌에 새긴 것입니다.
column2: It carves in stone the belief that Shiva bears in one body the three faces of creating, preserving and destroying.

column2: Portuguese soldiers used this cave for target practice, smashing many of the carvings. The stone elephant at the landing cracked too.

column2: A huge boulder is wedged over a split in the rock, forming a roof. From the cave floor to the roof stone is about five times a man's height.

column2: The walls are thickly pecked with people, animals, wheels and strange patterns. A crowned figure's headdress spreads like a fan.

column2: Among the pictures are mixed old Tamil letters carved much later. Left by people long after those who carved the pictures.

column1: 붉은 바위가 밀림 위로 이백 미터 가까이 솟았고, 꼭대기는 판판하여 궁궐과 물탱크를 둘 만큼 넓습니다.
column2: The red rock rises nearly two hundred meters above the jungle, and its top is flat and wide enough for a palace and water tanks.

column1: 바위 중턱 벽화 속 여인들은 구름 위에서 꽃을 들고, 몸이 금빛과 붉은빛으로 빛납니다. 허리 아래는 구름에 가려졌습니다.
column2: The women in the fresco halfway up the rock hold flowers above the clouds, their bodies glowing gold and red. Below the waist they're hidden by clouds.

column2: The women in the fresco halfway up the rock hold flowers above the clouds, their bodies glowing gold and red. Below the waist they're hidden by clouds.

column1: 아버지를 죽이고 왕이 된 카샤파가 아우 목갈라나의 복수를 두려워해 이 바위에 성을 쌓았습니다. 결국 싸움에서 지고 스스로 목숨을 끊었습니다.
column2: Kashyapa, who killed his father to become king, built a fortress on this rock fearing the revenge of his brother Moggallana. In the end he lost the battle and took his own life.

column2: The only way up is a narrow stair clinging to the rock face. Just roll stones from above and no army below can climb.

column2: The only way up is a narrow stair clinging to the rock face. Just roll stones from above and no army below can climb.

column1: 땅속으로 일곱 층을 내려가며 계단과 기둥 회랑이 이어지고, 맨 아래 둥근 우물까지 사람 키의 열다섯 배쯤 됩니다.
column2: Stairs and pillared galleries descend seven stories underground, and it's about fifteen times a man's height down to the round well at the bottom.

column2: Stairs and pillared galleries descend seven stories underground, and it's about fifteen times a man's height down to the round well at the bottom.

column1: 벽마다 비슈누의 열 화신과 춤추는 여인 조각 수백 개가 빼곡합니다. 진흙에 묻혔던 덕에 코와 손가락이 덜 깨졌습니다.
column2: Every wall is crowded with hundreds of sculptures of Vishnu's ten avatars and dancing women. Thanks to being buried in mud, noses and fingers were less broken.

column2: A well dug deep underground so water could be drawn even in the dry season. The shade of the stairs is cool, so people rested here at midday.

column2: A well dug deep underground so water could be drawn even in the dry season. The shade of the stairs is cool, so people rested here at midday.

column1: 왕비 우다야마티가 남편 비마 왕을 기려 지었다고 합니다. 남편을 기려 아내가 우물을 지은 것이 드뭅니다.
column2: They say Queen Udayamati built it in memory of her husband, King Bhima. It's rare for a wife to build a well in her husband's memory.

column1: 가장 큰 시바의 얼굴은 머리 장식까지 사람 키의 다섯 배가 넘습니다. 바위 벼랑을 통째로 얼굴로 깎았습니다.
column2: The largest face of Shiva, headdress included, is more than five times a man's height. They carved the whole rock cliff into a face.

column2: The largest face of Shiva, headdress included, is more than five times a man's height. They carved the whole rock cliff into a face.

column2: They say gods who failed to rise before sunrise were turned to stone by Shiva's curse. One short of ten million — hence "Unakoti."

column2: Every face is covered with moss and ferns, as if wearing a green beard. The rocks wet from the stream gleam black when the sun hits.

column2: Divine images are scattered on the cliffs on both sides of the valley where a stream flows, and a half-buried bull statue lies prone by the water.

column2: The inscription on the silver cup beside him has some twenty-six letters, and no one can read them. A rare script left by the steppe people.

column2: He wore at his waist a gold-decorated iron sword and a dagger. A young noble, but surely a warrior who went to battle.

column2: People with heads glowing round like suns stand with both hands raised. Rays are pecked dot by dot around their heads.

column2: The rock surface looks scorched black because ages of sun and rain have rusted its skin. Only the pecked spots show bright.

column2: Below the sun-headed people are people holding hands and dancing. A dance offered to the sun god.

column2: Below the sun-headed people are people holding hands and dancing. A dance offered to the sun god.

column2: Thousands of pictures cluster on the cliffs on both sides of the valley, and a spring flows down the valley — a good place for people to gather.

column2: The tall woman's artificial eyeball was molded round from bitumen, with the pupil and rays drawn in fine gold thread. Holes were bored round the eye to tie it on with cord.

column2: On a clay cup, a goat leaping at a tree to nibble leaves is painted in five stages. Turn the cup and the goat seems to move.

column2: From a grave came a child whose skull bears a hole that was drilled and healed. The skill of a healer from very ancient times.

column2: The Helmand River can't reach the sea and pools into lakes in this basin. Each time the river changed course, the city must have lost its water.

column2: Inside the walls are an altar for burning fire and a great pool of water. A people who worshipped fire and water together.

column2: The gold and silver ornaments from the graves are carved with eagles, snakes and ibex, and the cartwheels are fitted wood studded with copper nails.

column2: Along where the old Murghab channel dried up, mud-brick walls enclose a square, with round towers at every corner.

column2: When a river changes course, a desert city like this loses its lifeline overnight. Even now the nearest water is toward Merv.

column2: The golden crown hangs countless thin gold leaves so it trembles and sparkles like foliage with every step. It can be folded and carried.

column2: Over twenty thousand pieces of gold alone. With Roman coins, Indian ivory combs and Chinese mirrors mixed in, it's wealth from the very heart of the Silk Road.

column2: They say it's where King Siliwangi tried to build a palace in a single night but stopped when the cock crowed and day broke.

column2: The warty pigs and little buffalo painted here are animals that still live only on this island. Even the warts on the faces are drawn.

column2: Limestone peaks rise like a forest with hundreds of caves beneath them. Every cave has paintings, so seeing them all would take days.

column2: The entrance is so wide it's as if the mountainside were scooped out, about sixty meters high. It could hold several churches with room to spare.

column2: The swiftlet nests on the ceiling are the "yanwo" that Chinese merchants buy at the price of gold. They're gathered by climbing poles up to the ceiling.

column2: The red figures on the walls of the "Painted Cave" are the dead traveling to the afterworld by boat. Same meaning as the boat-shaped coffins on the floor.

column2: Bat droppings are piled knee-high, the smell is strong and the floor slippery. Cover your nose with cloth to go in.

column2: The flat top surface and the holes are aligned east-west, so some say it was a platform for watching the stars.

column2: The locals call it the stone boat the gods rode down from heaven, and don't climb on it lightly.

column2: Six pits are set neatly in two rows, and in one pit remains the base of a chestnut pillar more than a full armspan round.

column2: The flat clay figures have cross-shaped bodies with just round eyes and mouths pierced. Patterns made by rolling twisted cord wrap every pot.

column2: Chestnut shells, fish bones and wild-grape seeds pour out of the rubbish heaps. A village that planted and tended chestnut trees and ate its fill.

column2: A single longhouse is over thirty paces long, so dozens must have wintered together. They knew how to stay long in deep-snow country.

column2: A line through the centers of the two rings points to the summer solstice sunset. The larger ring is some forty paces across.

column2: The sundial-like spot inside the ring has one long stone set upright in the center with small stones laid round it like spokes.

column2: The river stones are all bluish stones from the nearby river. They deliberately chose stones of the same color and carried them here.

column2: The clay figures are all buried with broken legs or arms. Perhaps magic to transfer an ailing body part to the figure and break it.

column2: The keyhole tomb is about two hundred eighty meters long, its square front part short and its round rear part high.

column2: Old records say people stood in a line and passed the stones of Mount Osaka from hand to hand.

column2: More than two hundred square caves are bored tier upon tier into the soft tuff cliff. Each entrance is big enough to crawl into.

column2: They carved leaving a stone ledge like a bed inside each cave. The stone is soft, so they must have dug easily with iron chisels.

column2: The townsfolk say these were the homes of the Koropokkur, little people who live under butterbur leaves.

column2: On the cave walls grows a moss that glitters green when the light hits it. A moss that lives only in shady, damp caves.

column2: Stone men, stone horses and stone shields were carved from soft tuff. The stone is soft, so the work is delicate but easily broken too.

column2: They say Iwai, ruler of Tsukushi, fought against the court and lost, and the angry soldiers smashed the stone men he'd prepared in life.

column1: 쓰쿠시의 임금 이와이가 조정에 맞서 싸우다 졌고, 화가 난 군사들이 그가 살아서 마련해 둔 돌사람을 부수었다고 해요.
column2: They say Iwai, ruler of Tsukushi, fought against the court and lost, and the angry soldiers smashed the stone men he'd prepared in life.

column1: 돌방패와 돌칼이 가지런히 늘어선 모습이 무덤을 지키는 군사의 진 같습니다. 이와이가 지닌 군세를 자랑한 것입니다.
column2: The stone shields and swords lined up in order look like an army guarding the tomb. Iwai was showing off the forces he commanded.

column1: 돌방패와 돌칼이 가지런히 늘어선 모습이 무덤을 지키는 군사의 진 같아요. 이와이가 지닌 군세를 자랑한 것이에요.
column2: The stone shields and swords lined up in order look like an army guarding the tomb. Iwai was showing off the forces he commanded.

column1: 무덤 옆에 네모난 마당이 따로 붙어 있습니다. 재판하는 관리와 무릎 꿇은 도둑의 돌상이 섰던 자리입니다.
column2: A square courtyard is attached beside the tomb. It's where stone statues of an official holding court and a kneeling thief once stood.

column1: 무덤 옆에 네모난 마당이 따로 붙어 있어요. 재판하는 관리와 무릎 꿇은 도둑의 돌상이 섰던 자리예요.
column2: A square courtyard is attached beside the tomb. It's where stone statues of an official holding court and a kneeling thief once stood.

column1: 칼날 모양 돌기둥에 송곳니를 드러낸 신을 새겼는데, 머리카락이 뱀으로 꿈틀거립니다. 사람 키의 두 배가 넘는 화강암입니다.
column2: A fanged god is carved on the blade-shaped stone pillar, its hair writhing as snakes. Granite more than twice a man's height.

column1: 칼날 모양 돌기둥에 송곳니를 드러낸 신을 새겼는데, 머리카락이 뱀으로 꿈틀거려요. 사람 키의 두 배가 넘는 화강암이에요.
column2: A fanged god is carved on the blade-shaped stone pillar, its hair writhing as snakes. Granite more than twice a man's height.

column1: 회랑 밑으로 물을 흘려보내면 신전 전체가 짐승처럼 울부짖었다고 합니다. 소라고둥 나팔도 여기서 불었을 것입니다.
column2: They say when water was sent rushing through the galleries below, the whole temple roared like a beast. Conch-shell trumpets were probably blown here too.

column1: 회랑 밑으로 물을 흘려보내면 신전 전체가 짐승처럼 울부짖었다고 해요. 소라고둥 나팔도 여기서 불었을 것이에요.
column2: They say when water was sent rushing through the galleries below, the whole temple roared like a beast. Conch-shell trumpets were probably blown here too.

column1: 빛이 들지 않는 미로를 지나 신을 만나게 했습니다. 산페드로 선인장 즙을 마시고 신을 보았다고도 합니다.
column2: They made people pass through a lightless maze to meet the god. Some say they drank San Pedro cactus juice and saw the god.

column1: 빛이 들지 않는 미로를 지나 신을 만나게 했어요. 산페드로 선인장 즙을 마시고 신을 보았다고도 해요.
column2: They made people pass through a lightless maze to meet the god. Some say they drank San Pedro cactus juice and saw the god.

column1: 두 강이 만나는 골짜기 밑에 세워, 산 위와 바닷가와 밀림 쪽에서 오는 길이 모두 이곳에서 만납니다.
column2: It was built at the bottom of a valley where two rivers meet, so the roads from the mountains, the coast and the jungle all meet here.

column1: 두 강이 만나는 골짜기 밑에 세워, 산 위와 바닷가와 밀림 쪽에서 오는 길이 모두 이곳에서 만나요.
column2: It was built at the bottom of a valley where two rivers meet, so the roads from the mountains, the coast and the jungle all meet here.

column1: 모래 언덕으로 보이는 것이 모두 계단 피라미드입니다. 가장 큰 것은 높이가 사람 키의 열다섯 배쯤 됩니다.
column2: What look like sand dunes are all stepped pyramids. The biggest is about fifteen times a man's height.

column1: 모래 언덕으로 보이는 것이 모두 계단 피라미드예요. 가장 큰 것은 높이가 사람 키의 열다섯 배쯤 돼요.
column2: What look like sand dunes are all stepped pyramids. The biggest is about fifteen times a man's height.

column1: 무너진 벽 사이에서 펠리컨과 콘도르 뼈로 깎은 피리가 서른 개 넘게 나왔습니다. 다섯 구멍짜리 피리입니다.
column2: More than thirty flutes carved from pelican and condor bone came out from among the collapsed walls. Five-holed flutes.

column1: 무너진 벽 사이에서 펠리컨과 콘도르 뼈로 깎은 피리가 서른 개 넘게 나왔어요. 다섯 구멍짜리 피리예요.
column2: More than thirty flutes carved from pelican and condor bone came out from among the collapsed walls. Five-holed flutes.

column1: 돌을 갈대 그물 자루에 담아 그대로 쌓았습니다. 지진에도 자루가 흔들림을 받아 주어 무너지지 않았습니다.
column2: They packed stones into reed-mesh bags and stacked them as they were. In earthquakes the bags absorbed the shaking, so the walls didn't collapse.

column1: 돌을 갈대 그물 자루에 담아 그대로 쌓았어요. 지진에도 자루가 흔들림을 받아 주어 무너지지 않았어요.
column2: They packed stones into reed-mesh bags and stacked them as they were. In earthquakes the bags absorbed the shaking, so the walls didn't collapse.

column1: 바닷가 사람들의 마른 멸치와 이 골짜기의 목화를 서로 바꾸었습니다. 매듭 끈이 장부였을 것입니다.
column2: They traded the coastal people's dried anchovies for this valley's cotton. Knotted cords must have been their ledgers.

column1: 바닷가 사람들의 마른 멸치와 이 골짜기의 목화를 서로 바꾸었어요. 매듭 끈이 장부였을 것이에요.
column2: They traded the coastal people's dried anchovies for this valley's cotton. Knotted cords must have been their ledgers.

column1: 성의 들어가는 문이 세 개뿐인데, 안쪽으로 갈수록 좁아져 한 사람씩만 지나갈 수 있습니다. 지키기에 아주 좋은 성입니다.
column2: The fortress has only three entrances, narrowing as you go in until only one person at a time can pass. A superb fortress to defend.

column1: 성의 들어가는 문이 세 개뿐인데, 안쪽으로 갈수록 좁아져 한 사람씩만 지나갈 수 있어요. 지키기에 아주 좋은 성이에요.
column2: The fortress has only three entrances, narrowing as you go in until only one person at a time can pass. A superb fortress to defend.

column1: 산등성이 위 성벽의 길이가 육백 미터에 가깝고, 높이는 사람 키의 열 배쯤 됩니다.
column2: The walls atop the ridge are nearly six hundred meters long and about ten times a man's height.

column1: 산등성이 위 성벽의 길이가 육백 미터에 가깝고, 높이는 사람 키의 열 배쯤 돼요.
column2: The walls atop the ridge are nearly six hundred meters long and about ten times a man's height.

column1: 둥근 돌집마다 마름모와 지그재그 무늬 띠를 돌로 짜 넣었습니다. 무늬가 집 둘레를 한 바퀴 감습니다.
column2: Bands of diamond and zigzag patterns are worked into the stone of every round house. The pattern wraps once round the house.

column1: 둥근 돌집마다 마름모와 지그재그 무늬 띠를 돌로 짜 넣었어요. 무늬가 집 둘레를 한 바퀴 감아요.
column2: Bands of diamond and zigzag patterns are worked into the stone of every round house. The pattern wraps once round the house.

column1: 구름 속에 살던 차차포야 사람들이 쌓았습니다. 그들은 잉카에 꺾인 뒤 에스파냐 사람과 손잡고 잉카에 맞섰다고 합니다.
column2: It was built by the Chachapoya, who lived in the clouds. They say after being subdued by the Inca, they joined the Spaniards against the Inca.

column1: 구름 속에 살던 차차포야 사람들이 쌓았어요. 그들은 잉카에 꺾인 뒤 에스파냐 사람과 손잡고 잉카에 맞섰다고 해요.
column2: It was built by the Chachapoya, who lived in the clouds. They say after being subdued by the Inca, they joined the Spaniards against the Inca.

column1: 현무암 덩이를 쇠 연장 없이 돌망치로 쪼아 두툼한 입술과 납작한 코를 새겼습니다. 돌머리 하나가 수십 톤입니다.
column2: The basalt boulder was pecked with stone hammers, without iron tools, into thick lips and a flat nose. A single stone head weighs dozens of tons.

column1: 현무암 덩이를 쇠 연장 없이 돌망치로 쪼아 두툼한 입술과 납작한 코를 새겼어요. 돌머리 하나가 수십 톤이에요.
column2: The basalt boulder was pecked with stone hammers, without iron tools, into thick lips and a flat nose. A single stone head weighs dozens of tons.

column1: 근처 수십 리 안에 그만한 돌이 없습니다. 북서쪽 툭스틀라 화산 산에서 뗏목으로 강과 바다를 따라 날라 왔을 것입니다.
column2: There's no stone like it within dozens of li. It must have been brought by raft along rivers and sea from the volcanic Tuxtla mountains to the northwest.

column1: 근처 수십 리 안에 그만한 돌이 없어요. 북서쪽 툭스틀라 화산 산에서 뗏목으로 강과 바다를 따라 날라 왔을 것이에요.
column2: There's no stone like it within dozens of li. It must have been brought by raft along rivers and sea from the volcanic Tuxtla mountains to the northwest.

column1: 돌머리가 쓴 투구 같은 모자는 공놀이를 할 때 쓰는 가죽 모자를 닮았습니다. 공놀이 우두머리의 얼굴일지도 모릅니다.
column2: The helmet-like cap the stone head wears resembles the leather caps worn in the ball game. Perhaps the face of a ball-game champion.

column1: 돌머리가 쓴 투구 같은 모자는 공놀이를 할 때 쓰는 가죽 모자를 닮았어요. 공놀이 우두머리의 얼굴일지도 몰라요.
column2: The helmet-like cap the stone head wears resembles the leather caps worn in the ball game. Perhaps the face of a ball-game champion.

column1: 푸른 비취 도끼를 십자 모양으로 늘어놓고 묻은 구덩이가 있습니다. 땅속에 바친 제물입니다.
column2: There's a pit where blue-green jade axes were laid out in a cross and buried. An offering to the earth.

column1: 푸른 비취 도끼를 십자 모양으로 늘어놓고 묻은 구덩이가 있어요. 땅속에 바친 제물이에요.
column2: There's a pit where blue-green jade axes were laid out in a cross and buried. An offering to the earth.

column1: 신상마다 송곳니를 드러냈고, 어떤 것은 등에 또 하나의 짐승이 올라탄 이중 신상입니다. 화산 바위를 깎았습니다.
column2: Every idol bares its fangs, and some are double idols with another beast riding on their backs. Carved from volcanic rock.

column1: 신상마다 송곳니를 드러냈고, 어떤 것은 등에 또 하나의 짐승이 올라탄 이중 신상이에요. 화산 바위를 깎았어요.
column2: Every idol bares its fangs, and some are double idols with another beast riding on their backs. Carved from volcanic rock.

column1: 아이를 안은 신상과 새를 머리에 인 신상이 무덤 입구를 지킵니다. 죽은 이를 저승으로 이끄는 수호신일 것입니다.
column2: Idols holding a child and idols with birds on their heads guard the tomb entrances. Probably guardian gods who lead the dead to the afterworld.

column1: 아이를 안은 신상과 새를 머리에 인 신상이 무덤 입구를 지켜요. 죽은 이를 저승으로 이끄는 수호신일 것이에요.
column2: Idols holding a child and idols with birds on their heads guard the tomb entrances. Probably guardian gods who lead the dead to the afterworld.

column1: 막달레나 강이 처음 솟는 고원이라 사방 골짜기에서 물이 흘러내립니다. 신상이 언덕마다 흩어져 있습니다.
column2: It's the plateau where the Magdalena River first springs, so water flows down from valleys on every side. Idols are scattered across every hill.

column1: 막달레나 강이 처음 솟는 고원이라 사방 골짜기에서 물이 흘러내려요. 신상이 언덕마다 흩어져 있어요.
column2: It's the plateau where the Magdalena River first springs, so water flows down from valleys on every side. Idols are scattered across every hill.

column1: 샘터 바위 바닥에 뱀과 도마뱀 모양 물길을 새겨, 물이 그 몸을 따라 흐르게 했습니다.
column2: Channels shaped like snakes and lizards are carved into the rock floor of the spring, so the water flows along their bodies.

column1: 샘터 바위 바닥에 뱀과 도마뱀 모양 물길을 새겨, 물이 그 몸을 따라 흐르게 했어요.
column2: Channels shaped like snakes and lizards are carved into the rock floor of the spring, so the water flows along their bodies.

column1: 부리타카 강에서 산등성이까지 돌계단 천이백 개를 올라야 첫 마당에 닿습니다. 마당 수백 개가 계단처럼 이어집니다.
column2: You climb twelve hundred stone steps from the Buritaca River up the ridge to reach the first terrace. Hundreds of terraces follow one after another like stairs.

column1: 부리타카 강에서 산등성이까지 돌계단 천이백 개를 올라야 첫 마당에 닿아요. 마당 수백 개가 계단처럼 이어져요.
column2: You climb twelve hundred stone steps from the Buritaca River up the ridge to reach the first terrace. Hundreds of terraces follow one after another like stairs.

column1: 둥근 마당은 강돌로 테두리를 두르고 흙을 채워 평평하게 다졌습니다. 그 위에 나무와 짚으로 둥근 집을 지었습니다.
column2: The round terraces are edged with river stones, filled with earth and tamped flat. Round houses of wood and thatch were built on top.

column1: 둥근 마당은 강돌로 테두리를 두르고 흙을 채워 평평하게 다졌어요. 그 위에 나무와 짚으로 둥근 집을 지었어요.
column2: The round terraces are edged with river stones, filled with earth and tamped flat. Round houses of wood and thatch were built on top.

column1: 산사람 코기족은 이곳을 함부로 말하지 않습니다. 그들의 허락 없이 올라가면 길을 내주지 않을 것입니다.
column2: The Kogi, the mountain people, don't speak of this place lightly. Go up without their permission and they won't let you pass.

column1: 산사람 코기족은 이곳을 함부로 말하지 않아요. 그들의 허락 없이 올라가면 길을 내주지 않을 것이에요.
column2: The Kogi, the mountain people, don't speak of this place lightly. Go up without their permission and they won't let you pass.

column1: 밀림이 습하고 비가 잦아 돌계단이 미끄럽습니다. 강을 몇 번이나 건너야 하니 짐을 가볍게 꾸려야 합니다.
column2: The jungle is humid and it rains often, so the stone steps are slippery. We'll cross the river several times, so pack light.

column1: 밀림이 습하고 비가 잦아 돌계단이 미끄러워요. 강을 몇 번이나 건너야 하니 짐을 가볍게 꾸려야 해요.
column2: The jungle is humid and it rains often, so the stone steps are slippery. We'll cross the river several times, so pack light.

column1: 단단한 화강암을 쇠붙이 없이 더 단단한 돌로 쪼고 모래로 갈아 둥글게 다듬었습니다. 어느 방향으로 재도 지름이 거의 같습니다.
column2: The hard granite was pecked with even harder stone, no metal, and ground with sand into spheres. Measure any direction and the diameter is almost the same.

column1: 단단한 화강암을 쇠붙이 없이 더 단단한 돌로 쪼고 모래로 갈아 둥글게 다듬었어요. 어느 방향으로 재도 지름이 거의 같아요.
column2: The hard granite was pecked with even harder stone, no metal, and ground with sand into spheres. Measure any direction and the diameter is almost the same.

column1: 어떤 돌 공들은 줄지어 늘어서 있는데, 그 줄이 북쪽을 가리키거나 해가 뜨는 쪽을 가리킨다는 말이 있습니다.
column2: Some stone balls stand in rows, and there's talk that the rows point north or toward the sunrise.

column1: 어떤 돌 공들은 줄지어 늘어서 있는데, 그 줄이 북쪽을 가리키거나 해가 뜨는 쪽을 가리킨다는 말이 있어요.
column2: Some stone balls stand in rows, and there's talk that the rows point north or toward the sunrise.

column1: 이 고장 사람들은 천둥 신 타라가 바람의 신들을 쫓아내려 쏜 대포알이라 말합니다.
column2: The people here say they're cannonballs fired by Tara, the thunder god, to drive away the wind gods.

column1: 이 고장 사람들은 천둥 신 타라가 바람의 신들을 쫓아내려 쏜 대포알이라 말해요.
column2: The people here say they're cannonballs fired by Tara, the thunder god, to drive away the wind gods.

column1: 돌 공 속에 금이 들었다는 소문이 돌아 사람들이 깨뜨린 것이 여럿입니다. 깨진 공 속에는 돌뿐이었습니다.
column2: A rumor went round that there was gold inside the stone balls, and people smashed quite a few. There was only stone inside the broken ones.

column1: 돌 공 속에 금이 들었다는 소문이 돌아 사람들이 깨뜨린 것이 여럿이에요. 깨진 공 속에는 돌뿐이었어요.
column2: A rumor went round that there was gold inside the stone balls, and people smashed quite a few. There was only stone inside the broken ones.

column1: 손 자국이 붉고 검고 흰빛으로 겹겹이 찍혔습니다. 대부분 왼손이니 오른손으로 뼈 대롱을 쥐고 물감을 불었을 것입니다.
column2: Handprints are stamped layer on layer in red, black and white. Most are left hands, so they must have held a bone tube in the right hand and blown the paint.

column1: 손 자국이 붉고 검고 흰빛으로 겹겹이 찍혔어요. 대부분 왼손이니 오른손으로 뼈 대롱을 쥐고 물감을 불었을 것이에요.
column2: Handprints are stamped layer on layer in red, black and white. Most are left hands, so they must have held a bone tube in the right hand and blown the paint.

column1: 과나코 떼를 사냥꾼들이 에워싸고 공 달린 끈을 던지는 그림이 있습니다. 그 끈이 다리에 감기면 과나코가 넘어집니다.

column2: With Ming closing the seas and Japanese pirates swarming, there are almost no ships sailing straight from Hangzhou to Joseon. The only way back is on a Japanese ship.

column1: 주인은 그 손님이 고려 가는 배를 묻다가, 고려가 조선으로 바뀌었다는 말을 듣고 한참을 웃었다고 기억합니다.
column2: The owner remembers that guest asking for a ship to Goryeo, and laughing for a long time when told Goryeo had become Joseon.

column1: 스님은 그 나그네가 들려준 대로 박을 탈 때마다 「슬근슬근 톱질하세」 하는 가락까지 붙여 이야기합니다. 아이들이 그 대목을 가장 좋아합니다.
column2: The monk tells it just as that traveler did, even adding the tune "Seulgeun seulgeun, let's saw away" every time they saw open a gourd. The children love that part best.

column1: 이 땅에도 허리 부러진 참새를 고쳐 준 할머니가 박씨를 받는 옛이야기가 있습니다. 참새가 제비로, 할머니가 형제로 바뀐 것이 다릅니다.
column2: This land has an old tale too, of an old woman who mends a sparrow with a broken back and is given a gourd seed. The difference is the sparrow became a swallow and the old woman became brothers.

column2: This land has an old tale too, of an old woman who mends a sparrow with a broken back and is given a gourd seed. The difference is the sparrow became a swallow and the old woman became brothers.

column1: 사카이 배는 쓰시마를 거쳐 조선의 부산포로 건너갑니다. 그 사람도 쓰시마 배를 기다렸을 것입니다.
column2: Sakai ships cross by way of Tsushima to Busanpo in Joseon. That man must have waited for a Tsushima ship too.

column1: 사카이 배는 쓰시마를 거쳐 조선의 부산포로 건너가요. 그 사람도 쓰시마 배를 기다렸을 것이에요.
column2: Sakai ships cross by way of Tsushima to Busanpo in Joseon. That man must have waited for a Tsushima ship too.

column1: 스님은 다리 부러진 제비를 고쳐 준 마음이 부처의 자비와 같다며 이 이야기를 설법에 넣었다고 합니다.
column2: The monk says the heart that mended the swallow's broken leg is like the Buddha's compassion, and he put this story in his sermons.

column2: The monk says the heart that mended the swallow's broken leg is like the Buddha's compassion, and he put this story in his sermons.

column1: 지붕과 돌난간은 사진 속 모습과 똑같습니다. 다만 사진 속 뜰의 색색 옷 입은 사람들 대신 창을 든 군사가 서 있습니다.
column2: The roof and stone balustrades are exactly as in the photograph. Only, instead of the people in colorful clothes in the photo's courtyard, soldiers with spears stand there.

column2: The roof and stone balustrades are exactly as in the photograph. Only, instead of the people in colorful clothes in the photo's courtyard, soldiers with spears stand there.

column1: 봉투는 들기름 먹인 한지로 접었습니다. 물에 젖지 않고 벌레도 먹지 않아 두 해가 지나도 멀쩡합니다.
column2: The envelope is folded from hanji soaked in perilla oil. It doesn't get wet and bugs don't eat it, so it's intact even after two years.

column1: 봉투는 들기름 먹인 한지로 접었어요. 물에 젖지 않고 벌레도 먹지 않아 두 해가 지나도 멀쩡해요.

column1: 경복궁은 태조가 한양에 도읍을 정하고 처음 지은 궁궐입니다. 「큰 복을 누리라」는 뜻의 이름입니다.
column2: Gyeongbokgung is the first palace King Taejo built after making Hanyang his capital. Its name means "enjoy great blessings."

column1: 경복궁은 태조가 한양에 도읍을 정하고 처음 지은 궁궐이에요. 「큰 복을 누리라」는 뜻의 이름이에요.
column2: Gyeongbokgung is the first palace King Taejo built after making Hanyang his capital. Its name means "enjoy great blessings."

column1: 노승은 「푸른 눈 섞인 젊은이가 오면 주라」는 당부를 받고 두 해 동안 봉투를 간직했다고 합니다.
column2: The old monk says he was asked to "give this to a young man with a hint of blue in his eyes, should one come," and kept the envelope for two years.

column2: The old monk says he was asked to "give this to a young man with a hint of blue in his eyes, should one come," and kept the envelope for two years.

column1: 바위인 줄 알았던 살갗이 순식간에 붉게 변했습니다. 빛깔을 바꿔 숨는 재주가 오징어보다 몇 곱절 빠릅니다.
column2: The skin I took for rock turned red in an instant. Its knack for changing color to hide is several times faster than a squid's.

column1: 바위인 줄 알았던 살갗이 순식간에 붉게 변했어요. 빛깔을 바꿔 숨는 재주가 오징어보다 몇 곱절 빨라요.
column2: The skin I took for rock turned red in an instant. Its knack for changing color to hide is several times faster than a squid's.

column1: 팔 하나가 돛대만큼 굵습니다. 빨판에 붙잡히면 칼로 끊어 내야 하니 도끼를 갑판에 늘어놓아야 합니다.
column2: A single arm is as thick as a mast. If its suckers grab you, you'll have to hack free with a blade, so lay axes out on deck.

column1: 팔 하나가 돛대만큼 굵어요. 빨판에 붙잡히면 칼로 끊어 내야 하니 도끼를 갑판에 늘어놓아야 해요.
column2: A single arm is as thick as a mast. If its suckers grab you, you'll have to hack free with a blade, so lay axes out on deck.

column1: 안개 낀 섬 사이 바위 많은 물목에 숨어 기다립니다. 이 바다에서는 바위 가까이 붙어 가지 말아야 합니다.
column2: It hides and waits in rocky narrows between misty islands. In these waters, don't sail close to the rocks.

column1: 안개 낀 섬 사이 바위 많은 물목에 숨어 기다려요. 이 바다에서는 바위 가까이 붙어 가지 말아야 해요.
column2: It hides and waits in rocky narrows between misty islands. In these waters, don't sail close to the rocks.

column1: 머리에서 마지막 굴곡까지 어림해 보니 배 스무 척을 이은 것보다 깁니다. 몸이 물결처럼 솟았다 잠깁니다.
column2: By my reckoning from head to last coil, it's longer than twenty ships end to end. Its body rises and sinks like waves.

column1: 머리에서 마지막 굴곡까지 어림해 보니 배 스무 척을 이은 것보다 길어요. 몸이 물결처럼 솟았다 잠겨요.
column2: By my reckoning from head to last coil, it's longer than twenty ships end to end. Its body rises and sinks like waves.

column1: 올라우스 마그누스가 북방 해도 가장자리에 그려 넣은 바로 그 뱀입니다. 그림 속 붉은 갈기가 눈앞에서 흔들립니다.
column2: It's the very serpent Olaus Magnus drew at the edge of his chart of the north. The red mane in the picture is waving before my eyes.

column1: 올라우스 마그누스가 북방 해도 가장자리에 그려 넣은 바로 그 뱀이에요. 그림 속 붉은 갈기가 눈앞에서 흔들려요.
column2: It's the very serpent Olaus Magnus drew at the edge of his chart of the north. The red mane in the picture is waving before my eyes.

column1: 저 몸이 한 번 감기면 우리 배 늑골이 버티지 못합니다. 돛을 줄이고 옆으로 비켜 지나가야 합니다.
column2: If that body wraps round us once, our ship's ribs won't hold. Shorten sail and slip past to the side.

column2: If that body wraps round us once, our ship's ribs won't hold. Shorten sail and slip past to the side.

column1: 동쪽 바닷사람들은 이 용을 비와 바람의 주인으로 모십니다. 뱃머리에 향을 피우고 길을 비는 까닭을 이제 알겠습니다.
column2: The seafarers of the East revere this dragon as the master of rain and wind. Now I know why they burn incense at the bow and pray for safe passage.

column1: 동쪽 바닷사람들은 이 용을 비와 바람의 주인으로 모셔요. 뱃머리에 향을 피우고 길을 비는 까닭을 이제 알겠어요.
column2: The seafarers of the East revere this dragon as the master of rain and wind. Now I know why they burn incense at the bow and pray for safe passage.

column1: 청록 비늘에 금빛 뿔과 긴 수염이 번개에 번쩍입니다. 이 빛깔은 비단 그림의 용보다 훨씬 깊습니다.
column2: Blue-green scales, golden horns and long whiskers flash in the lightning. This color is far deeper than the dragons in silk paintings.

column1: 청록 비늘에 금빛 뿔과 긴 수염이 번개에 번쩍여요. 이 빛깔은 비단 그림의 용보다 훨씬 깊어요.
column2: Blue-green scales, golden horns and long whiskers flash in the lightning. This color is far deeper than the dragons in silk paintings.

column1: 용이 꼬리지느러미를 휘두르자 태풍의 눈 둘레로 물길이 갈라졌습니다. 그 고요한 틈으로 배를 대야 삽니다.
column2: When the dragon swung its tail fin, the water parted around the eye of the typhoon. We'll live only if we steer into that calm gap.

column1: 용이 꼬리지느러미를 휘두르자 태풍의 눈 둘레로 물길이 갈라졌어요. 그 고요한 틈으로 배를 대야 살아요.
column2: When the dragon swung its tail fin, the water parted around the eye of the typhoon. We'll live only if we steer into that calm gap.

column1: 삼각 이빨이 여러 줄로 나 있어 앞니가 빠지면 뒷줄 이빨이 앞으로 나옵니다. 물개 떼를 따라 이 물길에 머뭅니다.
column2: Its triangular teeth grow in many rows, so when a front tooth falls out, a tooth from the row behind moves forward. It stays in these waters following the seal herds.

column2: Its triangular teeth grow in many rows, so when a front tooth falls out, a tooth from the row behind moves forward. It stays in these waters following the seal herds.

column1: 주둥이의 흰 상처는 오래된 작살 자국입니다. 총알은 두꺼운 가죽에 튕기니 눈이나 아가미를 노려야 합니다.
column2: The white scar on its snout is an old harpoon wound. Bullets bounce off the thick hide, so aim for the eyes or gills.

column1: 주둥이의 흰 상처는 오래된 작살 자국이에요. 총알은 두꺼운 가죽에 튕기니 눈이나 아가미를 노려야 해요.
column2: The white scar on its snout is an old harpoon wound. Bullets bounce off the thick hide, so aim for the eyes or gills.

column1: 작은 배를 내리지 말고 피 묻은 미끼는 바다에 버리지 말라고 일러 두겠습니다. 냄새를 맡으면 끝까지 따라옵니다.
column2: I'll tell the men not to lower small boats and not to throw bloody bait into the sea. Once it catches the scent, it follows to the end.

column1: 작은 배를 내리지 말고 피 묻은 미끼는 바다에 버리지 말라고 일러 둘게요. 냄새를 맡으면 끝까지 따라와요.
column2: I'll tell the men not to lower small boats and not to throw bloody bait into the sea. Once it catches the scent, it follows to the end.

column1: 물 위에 그림자가 없습니다. 산 사람의 배가 아니니 부르는 소리에 대답하지 말고 기도를 올려야 합니다.
column2: It casts no shadow on the water. It's no ship of the living, so don't answer its calls — say your prayers.

column2: It casts no shadow on the water. It's no ship of the living, so don't answer its calls — say your prayers.

column1: 선체가 다 썩었는데도 세 돛대가 바람을 거슬러 섭니다. 이런 배가 물에 떠 있는 것은 조선의 이치로 설명할 수 없습니다.
column2: The hull is rotted through, yet three masts stand against the wind. No law of shipbuilding can explain such a ship staying afloat.

column2: The hull is rotted through, yet three masts stand against the wind. No law of shipbuilding can explain such a ship staying afloat.

column1: 포문에서 불 대신 찬 안개가 뿜어 나옵니다. 우리 포탄이 저 배를 꿰뚫을지 장담할 수 없습니다.
column2: Instead of fire, cold mist pours from its gunports. I can't promise our shot will pierce that ship.
